rule.name: Row-level consumer check for value-pinning tests
rule.trigger: A new or changed test asserts exact output values of a conversion, rounding, or special-value path: hex bit patterns, NaN/inf/denormal/negative-zero inputs, round-to-nearest vs truncation, tie cases, or any expectation table (std::array of pairs, GENERATE lists). Also any test comment containing 'today's', 'current', 'as it always did', 'preserve', 'a move/refactor must not change', or a design-doc row that says 'keep today's behavior'.
procedure: 1. List every expected-value row in the test hunks of the diff: grep -n -E '0x[0-9a-fA-F]{4,8}|->|std::pair|GENERATE' t/<file>.cpp over the added lines. Number the rows.

2. Classify each row: (A) bit-exact round trip, the expected value is the input itself; (B) a conversion or rounding policy, the expected value differs from the input by a rule (truncate, round, flush); (C) a special value (NaN, inf, denormal, -0, tie). Rows of class A pass this rule; continue with B and C.

3. For each B/C row, search the production tree for a consumer of that exact outcome: git grep -n -i '<keyword>' <head> -- h src (keywords: truncat, round, NaN, inf, the function name). Exclude t/, the design document, the PR body, and the moved doc comment of the function itself. A consumer is a kernel or reader that depends on the bit, a documented file or wire format, a user-visible output, or a Note that states the requirement with a reason. A comment that only says what the code does today ('exactly as X always did') is not a consumer.

4. For each C row, read the repository rules for that value class: grep -n -i 'NaN|inf|denormal' AGENTS.md t/AGENTS.md. If a rule treats the value as corruption or invalid, a row that asserts the path accepts, converts, or hides it contradicts the rule; mark it.

5. Check for a contradicting expectation elsewhere: git grep -n '<the same input bits>' <head> -- t h. Two tests pinning opposite policies for the same input (for example generic fp32s_to_bf16s keeps the NaN, the packed path turns it to +inf) means the rows pin an accident, not a contract.

6. Read the test's stated rationale (header comment, section name). If it is 'a move or refactor must not change this', note that behavior preservation of a move is a one-time check (compare outputs or run token identity once), not a durable CI assertion, unless step 3 found a consumer.

7. Report every B/C row with no consumer from step 3, every row flagged in step 4 or 5, and name the rows to keep (class A rows, and rows protecting an invariant another code path relies on, such as the partner-zero rows tied to Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots]).
8. Run the same steps on any test rows a review lens or critic PROPOSES to add; a proposal to pin a policy without a consumer is the same defect.
rule.discriminating_question: Name the production reader, format, documented requirement, or repo rule that breaks if this exact expected value changes. If the only answer is 'the implementation today' or 'the design table copied from the implementation', the row documents the implementation (AGENTS.md:35-38) and is a defect; if a consumer or rule is named, the row is a contract and stays.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag: class A rows (expected == input, bit-exact round trip); rows that protect an invariant another code path depends on with a cited Note (for example the partner-zero rows: kv_cache.hpp Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] explains NaN * 0 propagation); regression rows that reproduce a failure seen on main or in the product; rows pinning a documented wire, file, or hardware format; rows where a kernel comment states the policy difference and why (for example amx_attn_iface.hpp:65-79 on AVX truncation vs AMX rounding of P); rows in a test file dedicated to the conversion function itself (t_fp32.cpp testing fp32s_to_bf16s is the function's own contract). Do not flag a row only because its value is hex or because it concerns NaN; the flag needs a missing consumer or a contradicted rule.
rule.finding_template: t/<file>.cpp:<line>: this row makes '<input> stores as <output>' a tested contract. <Rule or absence>: AGENTS.md:<line> '<quoted rule>' / git grep '<keyword>' over h/ and src/ finds no reader that depends on <policy>; the only statement is the test comment '<quote>'. Drop the <named rows> and keep <the rows with a consumer: bit-exact round trip, partner-zero>.

votes.fix:
Name: Row-level consumer check for value- and structure-pinning tests.

Trigger: a test hunk in the diff adds or changes an assertion whose expected side is a literal (hex bit pattern, float, integer), an expectation table (std::array<std::pair<input, expected>>, parallel input/expected arrays), or a compile-time property (sizeof, alignof, std::is_*_v traits, operator presence or absence). Also fires on a test or design-document comment containing: today's, current, as it always did, preserve, must not change, a move/refactor must not.

Procedure:
1. List the rows. Take the added lines of the test hunks only. Keep lines that are REQUIRE/CHECK/STATIC_REQUIRE with a literal expected value, and the initializer lines of any expectation table (grep -n -E 'REQUIRE|CHECK|std::pair|std::array' on the added lines, then read each). Number the rows. Do not use '->' as a pattern.
2. Classify each row, in this precedence: (A) the expected value equals the input (bit-exact round trip, copy, move) -> passes, stop here for that row, even when the value is a NaN or inf; (B) the expected value is derived from the input by a rule the code chooses (truncate, round, flush, saturate, sign-handling); (C) the input is a special value (NaN, inf, denormal, -0, tie) and the output differs from it; (D) a structure or type property (size, alignment, trait, member presence).
3. Find the readers of the bits by data flow, not by keyword. Name the view type, accessor, or function the row stores through (for W1: v_vnni_view, page::get_v, page::v_packed::at). git grep -n '<that name>' <head> -- h src, exclude t/ and the function's own doc comment, and read each reader: does any branch, compare, pack, or format depend on the rounding policy or on the special value's post-conversion bits? Also read any Note the test or the function cites. Record one of: reader (file:line and what it depends on), documented format (file), repo rule (AGENTS.md line), user-visible contract (an API doc or wire format), or NONE. A comment that states the policy or its history ('exactly as X always did', 'keep today's behavior') is NONE. A numeric difference the repository already admits between its own paths (bf16 ulp from truncation vs round-to-nearest, see amx_attn_iface.hpp:65-79; add-order) is NONE: 'the logits or tokens would move by one ulp' is not a consumer.
4. For C rows, read AGENTS.md and t/AGENTS.md for the value class (grep -n -i 'NaN|inf|denormal'). Flag a row only when it asserts that the path turns the value into a different class (NaN -> inf or finite; inf -> finite; denormal -> zero with no documented flush policy). A row that keeps the value's class bit for bit is class A and already passed.
5. Check for a second policy on the same input. First read the test's own comments and the function's doc comment for 'would' / 'the generic X keeps' statements; they declare the second policy themselves. Then git grep the input literal over t/ and h/ and read each hit for whether it asserts a different output for the same conversion (an unrelated use, such as abs() in t_fp32.cpp:176, is not a second policy). Two policies for one input with no consumer for either = the row pins an accident.
6. For D rows: name the code that would fail to compile, allocate, or run if the property changed (for example an operator new[] path that relies on trivial construction, cited by Note). A static_assert already present in the production header is a duplicate; a property with no such code is structure-only.
7. Read the row's stated rationale. 'A move must not change this' justifies a one-time comparison before merge (a bit diff of the old and new path, or the token-identity run), not a CI assertion, unless step 3 or 6 named a consumer.
8. Report: every B/C/D row whose step 3/6 result is NONE, every row flagged in step 4 or 5, and the rows to keep (class A rows; rows with a named reader, Note, rule, or format; regression rows reproducing a failure seen on main or in the product).
9. Run steps 1-8 on rows a lens, critic, or design document PROPOSES; a proposal to pin a policy without a consumer is the same defect.

Discriminating question: Name the production reader, documented format, repo rule, or compatibility contract that breaks (wrong result, crash, format mismatch, rule violation) if this exact expected value or property changes. 'The implementation today', 'the design table', 'the output would differ by an admissible ulp', and 'the comment says so' are not answers. No answer = the row documents the implementation (AGENTS.md:35-38): defect. A named answer = contract: keep.

False-positive guard: do not flag class A rows; rows whose reader or Note is named in step 3/6 (partner-zero rows via Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots]; operand_range bounds via Note [BF16 matmul range] and host_matvec.hpp:71); regression rows with a cited failure; rows pinning a documented wire, file, or hardware format; rows in the unit test of the function itself (t_bf16.cpp for fp32s_to_bf16s, t_fp32.cpp for abs); rows where a production comment names the reader that needs the policy (a comment that only states the policy or its history does not count). Hex, NaN, or a table is never a reason by itself.

Finding template (Wade's register, no method): 't/<file>.cpp:<line>: this row makes "<input> stores as <output>" a tested contract. <AGENTS.md:<line> treats <value class> as <corruption/...>; this pins the path that <hides/converts> it.> The <named rows> likewise pin today's <rounding/structure>, with no named consumer. Suggest dropping <rows> and keeping <class A rows / rows with a consumer>.'

probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Row-level consumer check for value- and structure-pinning tests.

Trigger (narrowed): fire on an added or changed test assertion that is one of
(a) a VALUE row whose expected side is a literal or table entry that DIFFERS from the bits the test put in (a conversion, rounding, flush, saturation, or a special value changing class), or
(b) a STRUCTURE row: a STATIC_REQUIRE on a type's OWN member set, layout or traits (sizeof, alignof, is_trivially_*, is_default_constructible, is_convertible between the type's own const/non-const variants, presence or absence of operator[] or of a member call such as as_view() on a temporary).
Do NOT fire on: a row whose expected equals the input bits or equals bits the same test stored earlier (round trip, copy, at() read-back), whatever the value, NaN and inf included; a GENERATE list, a 'preserve/today/always did/must not change' word, or a hex literal by itself (these only point at rows to classify); a requires-expression probe that CALLS a production function (a kernel declaration, set_v, get_v) with a candidate argument type, whether it expects true or false, since it tests the call boundary the PR changes; a predicate with a size or alignment literal whose comment or Note names the reader that needs it (t_heap_v2.cpp:1213-1220 names the 64-byte vector and tile loads); a comparison against an independent formula or oracle (t_amx_numerics.cpp:228-238).

Procedure:
1. List rows: added lines matching REQUIRE|CHECK|STATIC_REQUIRE|std::pair|std::array, read each, number them. Never use '->' as a pattern.
2. Classify, in this precedence, stopping at the first match: A = expected == input bits or == bits the test stored earlier (keep, including partner-kept rows such as t_llama_unit.cpp:3594-3596, :3650); A' = a pair-invariant row (expected 0 for the untouched partner after an even write) whose test or stored-through function cites a Note (Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots], v_vnni.hpp:233-236, kv_cache.hpp:2227) -> keep; if the citation is missing, ask for it, do not drop; B = expected derived from the input by a policy the code chooses; B0 = a B row where the policy does not matter (the discarded bits are zero, so truncation and round-to-nearest agree: 1.0, 0.5, -2^-14, 0x7fc00000) -> not a policy pin, report only as 'goes with its section', never as the defect; C = a special value whose class changes (NaN -> inf or finite, inf -> finite, denormal -> zero); D = a structure row per trigger (b).
3. For B and C rows find readers by DATA FLOW: name the view type or accessor the row stores through (v_vnni_view, page::get_v, page::v_packed, load_row, copy_token), git grep that name over h/ and src/ excluding t/ and the function's own doc comment, read each reader, and record one of: reader file:line and what depends on the bits; documented format; AGENTS.md line; API or wire contract; NONE. A comment stating the policy or its history ('exactly as X always did', 'keep today's behavior') is NONE. A difference the repository already admits between its own paths (one bf16 ulp from truncation vs round-to-nearest, amx_attn_iface.hpp:65-79; add order) is NONE: 'tokens could move by an ulp' is not a consumer.
4. For C rows read AGENTS.md and t/AGENTS.md for the value class (grep -n -i 'NaN|inf|denormal'). Flag only a class change that the rule treats as hiding corruption (AGENTS.md:73-75: NaN is corruption, infinities may be valid identities, so NaN -> +inf hides corruption). A NaN that stays a NaN is A or B0 and already passed.
5. Second policy: first read the test's own comments and the function's doc comment for 'would' or 'the generic X keeps' statements (they declare it: t_llama_unit.cpp:3478-3479, :3570-3571); then grep the input literal or the conversion function name over t/ h/ src/ and read each hit (bf16.hpp:57-69 is the second policy here; an unrelated use such as abs() in t_fp32.cpp:176 is not). Two policies and no consumer for either = the row pins an accident.
6. For D rows: (i) if the row's subject is a trait or layout that a production static_assert on the same type or its container already asserts (kv_cache.hpp:1553-1556, :1594-1599, :2339-2342 for v_vnni_tensor and kv_block), it is a duplicate -> drop; (ii) else name the production code or Note that depends on the property (operator new[] creation path, Note [KV block lifetime] kv_cache.hpp:1441); none -> structure-only -> drop; (iii) a probe that calls a production function with a candidate type is NOT a D row (trigger exclusion) and is kept as the API-boundary contract.
7. Read the row's stated rationale. 'A move must not change this' justifies a one-time comparison before merge (bit diff of old and new path, or the token-identity run), not a CI assertion, unless step 3 or 6 named a dependent.
8. Report: every B (not B0) and C row with NONE from step 3, every row marked in step 4 or 5, every D row dropped in step 6; name the kept rows (A, A', API-boundary probes, rows with a named reader, Note, rule or format, regression rows with a cited failure). Do not list B0 rows as findings.
9. Apply steps 1-8 to rows a lens, critic or design document PROPOSES to add; a proposed policy pin without a consumer is the same defect.

Discriminating question: name the production reader, documented format, repo rule or compatibility contract that gives a wrong result, crashes, mismatches a format, or breaks a rule if this exact expected value or property changes. 'The implementation today', 'the design table', 'the comment says so', 'the output would differ by an admissible ulp', and 'nothing would fail to compile but the type would be less safe' (that last one marks an API-boundary probe, which is kept, not a structure row) are not answers. No answer = the row documents the implementation (AGENTS.md:35-38): defect. A named answer = contract: keep.

False-positive guard (explicit): never flag class A rows, including NaN, inf and -0 round trips (t_llama_unit.cpp:3524-3563, :3657-3696); never flag pair-invariant rows with a Note (partner-zero :3541-3545, :3632-3638); never flag requires-expression probes that call a kernel or cache function, positive or negative (:383-391, and constructibility probes that encode 'a bare pointer is not a plane view' :394-397 when the PR body or issue states that contract); never flag an at()/read-back section (:3700-3708); never flag an oracle comparison (t_amx_numerics.cpp:228-238); never flag a size or alignment predicate whose comment names its reader (t_heap_v2.cpp:1220); never flag a row in the unit test of the conversion function itself (t_bf16/t_fp32 for fp32s_to_bf16s); never list B0 rows as the defect. A GENERATE, a 'preserve' word, hex, or NaN is never a reason by itself. Duplicate-coverage (W5) and misnamed-section (W6) findings belong to other rules.

Finding template (Wade's register, no method): 't/<file>.cpp:<line>: this row makes "<input> stores as <output>" a tested contract. rule.name: Contract check runs where CI runs, with an oracle the code under test cannot bias
rule.trigger: A diff adds or moves an assertion whose comment or PR body calls it the check of a layout, formula, address, or contract (words: 'independent', 'formula', 'layout', 'must equal', 'bit-exact', 'address'); OR a diff adds assertions inside a Catch2 TEST_CASE that contains an early 'return' or SKIP guarded by a runtime capability probe (available(), cpuinfo flags, FPGA presence, env var, min_slices); OR a test's expected value is computed by a helper that the production path also calls.
procedure: 1. List the new or moved REQUIRE/CHECK lines in the diff: `git diff <base> <head> -- t/ | grep -n '^+.*\(REQUIRE\|CHECK\|STATIC_REQUIRE\)'`. For each, open the full file at <head> (`git show <head>:t/<file>`), not the hunk.

2. Walk upward from each assertion to the start of its TEST_CASE. Note every statement that can exit early: `grep -n 'return;\|SKIP(\|WARN(\|available()\|getenv\|#if' t/<file>`. Record the condition for each gate above the assertion.

3. For each gate, decide what it depends on: build flag (TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_CHUNK_SIZE), host hardware (AMX, FPGA, slices), environment variable, or data. Then check the CI hosts: `git show <main>:.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml | grep -n 'runs-on\|DTRON_'` and the runner inventory (README.ci.md, memory amx-ci-coverage-facts.md: AMD andoria runners have no AMX; .passed cache may skip the test step). If any CI host fails the gate, the assertion does not run there.

4. Ask whether the assertion needs that gate: does the code between the gate and the assertion call the gated hardware? In W2 the byte comparison calls append_v_row and memcpy only; the kernel call comes after it. If the assertion does not need the gate, it is misplaced.

5. Find the oracle of the assertion (the expression on the expected side). Trace every function it calls: `grep -n '<helper>' h/ t/`. If the expected side and the actual side reach the same helper (here pair_base via at() and append_v_row), the assertion cannot detect a fault in that helper. Write down the shared helper by name.

6. Mutation step (do it on paper, or in a scratch copy, never in the worktree): change the shared helper in one way (for example multiply the pair-row stride by 2, or swap token parity). List which assertions in the whole test suite fail on a host WITHOUT the gated hardware. If the list is empty, the contract is untested in CI.

7. Compare with the PR body and the test's own comments: any sentence that says the layout or formula is 'checked', 'verified', or 'holds' must name an assertion that survives steps 3-6. Quote the sentence and the assertion that backs it, or report the gap.

8. Report: the assertion line, the gate line, the CI hosts that skip it, the shared helper that makes other checks non-independent, and the cheapest move (above the gate in the same case, or into the closest existing non-gated test per AGENTS.md 'Prefer extending the closest existing test').
rule.discriminating_question: If the helper that computes the address (or the value) were wrong, which assertion would fail on a CI host that lacks the hardware this TEST_CASE gates on? If the answer is 'none', the contract is unprotected even though a check exists in the file.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag when the gated assertion genuinely needs the hardware (it consumes the output of a kernel call that sits above it) AND a second, non-gated assertion with an independent oracle covers the same contract elsewhere; name that second assertion before dismissing. Do not flag a shared helper when the expected side is a literal table, a hand-written formula, or data from a different implementation (an AVX reference against an AMX kernel is independent). Do not flag compile-time STATIC_REQUIREs for run-gate placement; they execute at build time on every CI lane that compiles the file.
rule.finding_template: t/<file>:<assert line>: this is the only comparison of <contract> against a formula that does not go through <shared helper>, but it sits after the <probe>() early return at :<gate line>, so it does not run on <CI hosts without the capability>. The <other test> section does not cover it: <side A> and <side B> both compute their address through <shared helper>, so a wrong <helper> passes both. Move the comparison above the early return, or into <closest non-gated test> as its own case.

votes.reason: The rule's discriminating question does not fire on the W2 defect it was derived from. The question asks "if the helper that computes the address (pair_base) were wrong, which assertion would fail on a CI host without AMX? If none, unprotected." The honest answer is not "none": the non-gated TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE "scaled_v" (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:1985-2090 at 96a6220ab6) writes every token through set_v -> append_v_row -> pair_base and reads it back through scaled_v_expr, whose address arithmetic is `data + i * head_size` on the plane pointer (kv_cache.hpp:2190/2268/2282, data = v_vnni_access::plane, not pair_base), then compares with the logical pattern. A wrong pair_base stride fails that test on AMD runners. So an agent applying the rule as written dismisses W2 (the finding template's clause "the only comparison ... that does not go through pair_base" is also literally false). What the gated check at t_amx_numerics.cpp:227 uniquely protects is different: conformance of the bytes to the DOCUMENTED formula that the AMX kernel consumes. Two AVX production routes (writer append_v_row, reader scaled_v_expr) agreeing with each other proves only that they agree; if both drift from the documented layout together, the AMX kernel misreads and no AMD-runner test fails. The rule must therefore ask about the oracle (hand-written formula vs. another production route), not about which helper is shared. Secondary executability problems: trigger clause 3 ("expected value computed by a helper the production path also calls") fires on representation helpers like to_bits/from_bits/bf16_rne that both sides legitimately use; step 6 ("list which assertions in the whole test suite fail", on paper) is not executable without a build and is replaced by a grep-based route classification; step 3 is executable (workflow runs-on at :381 is [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512], README.ci.md:443-452 shows the andoria runners carry no `intel` label and are AMD Genoa). The false-positive guard's second clause ("a second non-gated assertion with an independent oracle covers the same contract") would also admit scaled_v and must exclude production-route-vs-production-route comparisons. trigger (replace clause 3): (1) a diff adds or moves an assertion whose comment, Note, or PR body calls it the check of a layout, address formula, or byte contract (words: independent, formula, layout, must equal, bit-exact, documented); OR (2) a diff adds assertions below an early `return`, `SKIP(`, or `WARN(`+`return` guarded by a runtime capability probe (`available()`, cpuinfo flag, FPGA presence, min_slices, env var) in a Catch2 TEST_CASE; OR (3) a test's expected ADDRESS or INDEX (not a value conversion such as to_bits/from_bits/bf16_rne) is produced by a production accessor of the same storage (here `at()`), rather than by a literal or a formula written out in the test.

procedure (replace steps 5-6; keep 1-4, 7-8):
5. Name the oracle of each new assertion: literal table, hand-written formula in the test, output of a different implementation (AVX reference vs AMX kernel), or a production accessor/reader of the same storage. Only the first three are independent. A production reader (scaled_v_expr, get_v, at()) is a route, not an oracle, even when its address arithmetic differs from the writer's.
6. Name the consumer of the documented formula (grep the Note that states the formula, then grep its readers: `git grep -n 'v_packed\\|as_view()\\|pair_base\\|plane(' <head> -- h/ src/`). The contract is unprotected on a runner class if every non-gated assertion on that class compares two production routes with each other (writer vs reader) or shares the helper on both sides, and the gated assertion is the only one whose oracle is the formula itself. Do not claim the result of a mutation you did not compile; say which routes would and would not detect a stride fault, and which fault class (writer and reader drifting together) no non-gated route detects.

discriminating_question: Which non-gated assertion compares the stored bytes with the formula written out in the test or the Note, rather than with what another production accessor or reader returns? If the only such assertion sits below a capability gate, the formula that the gated consumer (the AMX kernel) relies on is unverified on every CI runner that fails the gate, even though writer/reader round-trip tests pass there.

Do not count a writer-vs-reader round trip (set_v then scaled_v or get_v) as an independent check of the formula: it proves the two routes agree, not that they agree with the layout the gated consumer assumes; say this explicitly when dismissing or keeping the finding. probe.tightened_rule:
name: A layout-formula check must execute on every CI runner class.

trigger (all three parts must hold; (a) selects candidates, (b) and (c) confirm):
(a) The diff adds a RUNTIME assertion (REQUIRE or CHECK; never STATIC_REQUIRE or static_assert) whose actual side is stored bytes or indices of a storage layout (a memcpy of an owner, raw plane elements, a packed index) and whose expected side is a literal table or a formula written out in the test or in a Note. A comment or PR-body sentence that says 'layout' or 'formula' about that assertion is a hint to look; it is not the trigger by itself. The words 'address', 'must', 'bits', 'contract' alone never trigger.
(b) Between the start of the TEST_CASE and that assertion there is a runtime exit (return, SKIP, or WARN plus return) conditioned on a hardware or environment probe (available(), cpuinfo flag, FPGA presence, min_slices, getenv), AND the statements between the exit and the assertion do not call the probed hardware. A compile-time '#if' is not a runtime exit; check instead whether the CI build sets the flag (grep -DTRON_ in the workflow).
(c) At least one CI runner class fails the probe (runner table in README.ci.md: an entry without the 'intel' label has no AMX), AND no other runtime assertion that executes on every runner class has the same oracle class (literal or formula vs stored bytes). To decide (c): list every non-gated TEST_CASE that touches the same storage (git grep the storage accessors over t/ at the head) and classify each assertion as (i) formula or literal vs stored bytes, (ii) writer-then-reader round trip (set_v then get_v, at(), scaled_v, copy), or (iii) two production readers compared with each other. Only class (i) substitutes. Classes (ii) and (iii) are route checks: they prove that the routes agree, not that they agree with the layout the gated consumer (the AMX kernel) assumes, whatever address helper each side uses.

discriminating question: Which runtime assertion that runs on every CI runner class compares stored bytes or indices with the formula written out in the test or the Note? If the only such assertion sits below a hardware-probe exit and does not need that hardware, report it, and name the route checks that do run everywhere and why they do not substitute.

false_positive_guard:
- Never flag a gated assertion that consumes the output of the gated call above it (QK/PV tolerance checks).
- Never flag compile-time checks under this rule; they run on every lane that compiles the file. Exclude them at the trigger, not at the report.
- Never flag a round-trip or reader-vs-reader section as its own finding. Sections whose stated contract is a value property (bit preservation, partner zeroing, fp32/fp16 truncation, copy parity, 'scaled_v must match get_v' cross-checks) have writer-then-reader through the same address helper as their correct oracle. Name them only inside a formula finding, as 'does not cover the formula because <writer> and <reader> both address through <helper>'.
- A predicate assertion (is_aligned, != nullptr, size ==) is not a layout comparison; its expected side is not a layout formula.
- One finding per gated formula assertion; the classification list from (c) is part of that finding, never a second finding.
- Before reporting, quote the PR body's own per-arm assertion counts when it gives them (an AMX-on count larger than the kill-switch count by the size of the comparison is direct proof of the skip without running anything).

finding_template (Wade's register: location, what the code does, one ask with two options): t/<file>:<assert line>: this is the only comparison of the <layout> bytes against the formula itself (<formula>), but it sits after the <probe>() early return at :<gate line>, so it does not run on <runner class without the capability>. <Other test> does not cover it: <writer route> and <reader route> both address through <shared helper> (or: they only check that two production routes agree), so a layout that drifts from the Note passes both while <gated consumer> still assumes the Note. Move the comparison above the early return, or into <closest non-gated test> as its own case.

rule.name: Guarantee claim vs enforcing declaration
rule.trigger: The PR body, a commit message, a Note, or a code comment states a compile-time or type-level guarantee over a SET of subjects: words such as 'compile error', 'cannot be passed', 'rejected', 'enforced', 'typed view', 'no bare/raw pointer', 'only through', 'tested with STATIC_REQUIRE/static_assert'. Also fires when a diff adds a `using X = <existing generic template><...>` alias and the body or a comment calls X 'typed' or 'a type'.
procedure: 1. Extract the claims. Run: grep -n -i -E 'compile error|cannot|reject|enforce|only (through|via)|no (bare|raw) pointer|typed|STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert' <pr-body.md> and the diff's comments. For each hit write one line: (subject set, forbidden input, claimed mechanism). Expand every plural or 'and' into its members (here: 'packed V plane' AND 'native K plane').

2. For each subject, find the boundary type. grep -n '<kernel or API name>(' h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (or the header the body names) and copy the parameter type. Resolve it: git show <head>:<file> and follow every `using` until a `struct`/`class` definition. Record: new class, or alias of a pre-existing generic template (e.g. view / const_view in h/tron/tensor/view.hpp).

3. For an alias of a generic template, list its public constructors: grep -n -E 'explicit|constexpr (view|const_view)\(|\bview\(|const_view\(' on the definition file. A public pointer constructor (even `explicit`) means any pointer constructs the type with a one-token wrap. Then check whether the same instantiation is produced elsewhere: grep -rn the template arguments (e.g. 'const_view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<page_size, head_size>>') in h/ src/ t/. Each other producer is a same-typed buffer that passes the boundary.

4. Read the cited tests. grep -n 'STATIC_REQUIRE' t/<file> around the probes the body cites. For each subject look for an assertion in the OPPOSITE direction (a positive is_constructible_v<Subject, T*> or is_same_v<Subject, GenericView>). A positive pointer-constructibility assertion on a subject the body says rejects pointers is the contradiction; quote it.
5. Grep call sites for a one-expression wrap: grep -rn -E '<AliasName><[^>]*>\{' h/ src/ t/. A wrap of a raw pointer at any call site (test or production) shows the pointer route is open.

6. Build a per-subject truth table with three rows: (a) raw pointer passed directly, (b) raw pointer wrapped in one expression, (c) same-shaped view of another buffer. Mark each 'rejected' / 'accepted' with the file:line that decides it. The body's sentence holds only if every subject reads 'rejected' in all three rows (or the body names the rows that are open).
7. Write the finding with the truth table, and ask for the body to be scoped and for the distinct type in the named follow-up, unless the body already states the limitation.
rule.discriminating_question: For every subject the sentence covers, is the forbidden input rejected because of a property of a type introduced for that subject (no public pointer constructor, a distinct class), or only because of a property shared with the pre-existing generic type (an `explicit` constructor) that a one-token wrap or a same-shaped view defeats?
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag when the body or Note already names the limitation for that subject ('names the layout but does not enforce it', 'alias of the existing view'). Do not flag when the subject set is explicitly limited to the subjects that have the distinct type. Do not flag `explicit` alone as a defect: the finding is the sentence's scope, not the constructor. Do not demand the distinct type in this PR when the author names a follow-up PR for it. Do not flag an alias introduced only to shorten spelling when nothing calls it a guarantee (that is ben-review territory).
rule.finding_template: `<alias>` (<fwd header:line>) is an alias of the generic `<template>` (<definition file:line>, public pointer constructor at <line>), and <test file:line> asserts it is constructible from `<ptr type>`; <call site file:line> wraps a raw pointer in one expression. So any pointer or same-shaped row-major view passes `<kernel>`; the description's '<quoted claim>' holds for <subjects with a distinct type> only. Say so in the description and give <subject> a distinct type in <follow-up PR>.

votes.fix:
Name: Guarantee claim vs enforcing declaration.

Trigger: a sentence in the PR body, a commit message, a Note, or a code comment that (a) names a rejected input ('bare pointer', 'raw pointer', 'the other plane's view', 'cannot be passed') AND (b) names a mechanism ('compile error', 'rejected', 'STATIC_REQUIRE', 'static_assert', 'enforced', 'no public pointer') over one or more subjects. A sentence with the word 'typed' but no rejected input is not a claim on its own; attach it to the nearest claim sentence about the same subject, or drop it.

Procedure:
1. Extract claims. grep -n -i -E 'compile error|cannot be passed|reject|enforce|no (bare|raw|public) pointer|STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert' on the body and on the diff's added comment lines. Keep only hits that name a rejected input. For each, write (subject list expanded member by member, rejected input, mechanism). Here: subjects = packed V plane, native K plane; input = bare pointer, other plane's view; mechanism = compile error via STATIC_REQUIRE.
2. Find each subject's boundary type. grep -n '<SubjectTypeName>' on the diff's added lines and take every function parameter that uses it (here const_native_k_view at amx_attn_iface.hpp and amx_attn.cpp). Resolve the parameter type with git show <head>:<file> through every `using` to a struct/class. Record whether it is a new class or an alias of a pre-existing generic template.
3. List the producers of that type, not just its constructors. (a) Constructors: read the class body and note the access specifier above each pointer constructor; a PUBLIC pointer constructor, explicit or not, is an open route (view.hpp:296 public vs v_vnni.hpp:130/137 private). (b) Friends and factory functions (v_vnni.hpp:131-134, as_view at :163-175). (c) Other instantiations of the same generic template: grep the template name plus element type (git grep -n 'const_view<bf16' h src t), not the alias's argument spelling, because defaults and `seq<>` aliases change the spelling (views.hpp:26). Settle identity for each hit with a compile probe `static_assert(std::is_same_v<Alias<64,128>, decltype(expr)>)` or by reading the default arguments. Each producer that does not itself guarantee the layout (built from a raw pointer, like kv_cache.hpp:2357) is an open route.
4. Read the cited tests. grep -n 'STATIC_REQUIRE' around the probes the body cites. For each subject, look for a positive is_constructible_v<Subject, T*> or is_same_v<Subject, GenericView>. Quote it as the contradiction when the body says the subject rejects pointers.
5. Grep call sites for a one-expression wrap: git grep -n -E '<AliasName><[^>]*>\{' <head> -- h src t. Any wrap of a raw pointer, in test or production, shows the pointer route is open.
6. probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Guarantee claim vs enforcing declaration.

Trigger (all three parts must hold for one sentence):
(a) The sentence is in the PR body, a commit message, a Note, or a code comment, and it names a REJECTED INPUT at a function or type boundary: 'bare pointer', 'raw pointer', 'bf16*', 'the other plane's view', 'cannot be passed', 'cannot be handed in'.
(b) The sentence names a compile-time mechanism: 'compile error', 'rejected', 'enforced', 'no public pointer', 'STATIC_REQUIRE', 'static_assert', 'tested with'.
(c) The sentence covers one or more subjects (expand every plural or 'and' into members; here: packed V plane, native K plane).
Not a trigger on its own: the word 'typed'; a `using` alias; an 'only through' access policy whose named exception is a test-only helper in the same header's Note; a property claim with no rejected input ('is trivially copyable', 'has alignment 64', 'same size as the array it replaces', 'checked by static_assert'); 'cannot' in a sentence about test visibility ('cannot see', 'cannot pass by coincidence'). A 'typed'-only sentence about the same subject is attached to the nearest trigger sentence as a second citation, never as its own finding.
Run the rule at the head submitted for review, and again whenever the body or a Note was edited after the last review of the code. For each subject also compare the claim against the design document's recorded limitations (grep -n -i -E 'still permits|remains legal|does not prove|limitation' on the design file) and quote any limitation the claim drops.

Procedure (unchanged in substance, with these corrections):
1. Keep only step-1 hits that satisfy trigger (a). Grep the diff's ADDED COMMENT lines, not code lines; static_assert and STATIC_REQUIRE lines are read in step 4, not extracted as claims.
2. Find the boundary parameter type by grepping the subject's type name in the diff's added lines and resolving every `using` with git show <head>:<file> to a struct or class.
3. List PRODUCERS, not only constructors: (a) every pointer constructor with the access specifier above it (public vs private: view.hpp:296 is public, v_vnni.hpp:130/137 is private); (b) friends and factory functions (as_view, v_source_row); (c) other instantiations of the same generic template, found by grepping the template name plus element type (`const_view<bf16`), because default arguments and `seq<>` change the spelling (kv_cache.hpp:2357 vs kv_cache_fwd.hpp:49). Settle identity by reading the defaults or by a compile probe.
4. Read the cited tests for a positive is_constructible_v<Subject, T*> or is_same_v<Subject, GenericView>; quote it as the contradiction.
5. Grep call sites for one-expression wraps of a raw pointer.
6. Truth table per subject, three rows: (a) raw pointer passed directly; (b) raw pointer wrapped in one expression through a public constructor, friend or factory; (c) a value of the type produced from a buffer that carries no layout guarantee (a producer from 3c built from a raw array). A second owner's view of the same type is NOT row (c) when that owner carries the layout. The claim holds for a subject when rows (b) and (c) both read 'rejected'; row (a) alone proves nothing, and an explicit constructor is never a defect by itself.
7. Group every claim location by subject and write ONE finding per failing subject, citing every location of the claim (body row, kernel-header comment, test comment).

Discriminating question: for each subject the sentence covers, can a raw pointer, or a view of a buffer that carries no layout guarantee, become the boundary parameter type in one expression through any public constructor, friend, factory, or other instantiation of the same generic template? If yes for any route, the compile-time claim does not hold for that subject, whatever the class's name and whether its constructor is explicit.

False-positive guard:
- Do not flag when the SAME sentence or the same table row states the limitation for that subject ('names the layout but does not enforce it', 'keeps its explicit pointer wrap'). Do not flag a test comment or a header comment when the same file within the same block states the limitation (t_llama_unit.cpp:392-393 clears :371-373 and the kernel probes). A limitation stated in a different file or a different body row does not clear the claim and is quoted as evidence for the finding.
- Do not flag a subject whose every producer carries the layout (V here: private constructor, owner's as_view only), even though a second owner's view of the same type passes.
- Do not flag a subject the sentence excludes by name or build configuration.
- Do not flag a `using` alias or a 'typed' wording that makes no rejection claim; that is ben-review territory.
- Do not demand the distinct type in this PR when a follow-up PR is named; ask for the scope of the sentence instead, and name the follow-up as the place for the distinct type.
- Do not issue a second finding for a second location of the same claim on the same subject; add it as a citation to the one finding.

Finding template (two sentences of fact, one of consequence, one ask): "`<alias>` is an alias of the generic `<template>` (<definition file:line>), and <test file:line> asserts it is constructible from `<ptr type>`. <call site file:line> wraps a raw pointer in one expression, and <producer file:line> builds the same type from the cache's raw array. So any pointer or same-shaped row-major view passes `<kernel>`; '<quoted claim>' holds for <subjects that pass> only. Fine as a first step, but please say so in <every location of the claim>, and give <subject> a distinct type in <follow-up PR>, or drop the claim for <subject>." Add, when the design document records the limitation: "The design already states this at <design file:line>; carry that sentence into the description."

rule.name: Structure-only compile-time test checks (consumer or duplicate test)
rule.trigger: The diff adds, in t/, any STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE / static_assert / REQUIRE whose operand is a type trait (std::is_*_v), sizeof, alignof, a requires-expression that probes the ABSENCE of a member, operator or constructor, or a comparison of a constant with the value a declaration already states (alignas N vs alignof == N, = delete vs not callable).
procedure: 1. List the added compile-time assertions in test files: grep -n '^+.*\(STATIC_REQUIRE\|static_assert\)' <pr.diff> | grep ' t/' (or git diff <base> <head> -- t/ | grep -n '^+.*STATIC_REQUIRE'). Record file:line at the reviewed head.

2. Classify each assertion. K = the requires-expression or expression calls a production function or kernel (e.g. amx_attn_h128g4::qk_rowmajor_128x4(...) inside requires). S = a type trait, sizeof, alignof, is_constructible/is_convertible/is_default_constructible, or a probe of a missing member or operator. Keep every K; continue with S only.

3. For each S, search the production headers for the same trait on the same type: git grep -n -E 'static_assert.*(is_trivially|is_default|is_constructible|is_convertible|sizeof|alignof)' -- h/ src/ | grep -i '<type-or-alias>'. Resolve aliases (v_storage = v_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size>; page_size = 64 at kv_cache.hpp:1750). A match on the same type and trait = duplicate.

4. For each S not a duplicate, open the class definition and check whether the assertion restates a declaration in the same class: alignas(N) on the struct vs alignof == N; `= delete` on the rvalue overload vs 'no view of a temporary'; absence of operator[] in the class body vs 'no operator[]'. A restatement with no caller is a tautology against the declaration.

5. For each remaining S, name the consumer: git grep -n -E '<type>.*\[|\[.*<type>' -- h/ src/ for operator[] uses; git grep -n 'v_vnni_view<[^>]*>\s*[a-z_]*;' for default constructions; for trivial-type traits find the production line that relies on the trait (the operator new[] object-creation path) and check whether that line's own file already static_asserts it (step 3). Read the comment above the test assertion: if it says 'no production code uses/reads this' or names a review thread or commit as the reason, mark the assertion as self-declared consumer-less.

6. Count: K kept; S duplicates, S tautologies, S consumer-less. Write one finding per test block that names the kept probes by line range and the droppable assertions by line, with the production static_assert file:line for each duplicate.

rule.discriminating_question: If this assertion flipped, which production line would misbehave, and is that line not already protected by a static_assert in its own header? If no such line exists, or it is already protected, the assertion only documents structure.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag a trait check when production code relies on the trait and NO production header asserts it (then the finding is 'move the static_assert into the header', not 'drop the test'). Do not flag probes that invoke a production function or kernel in a requires-expression (K probes): they protect the signature the PR exists to introduce. Do not flag a sizeof/alignof check that pins an ABI or on-disk/DMA layout consumed by code outside the type's own header (a hardware descriptor, a wire format) when no header asserts it. Do not count pre-existing assertions outside the diff as PR findings; mention them only as context.

votes.fix:
name: Structure-only compile-time checks in tests (boundary probe, or shape of a helper type)

trigger: The diff adds in t/ a STATIC_REQUIRE, STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE, static_assert, or REQUIRE whose operand is a type trait (std::is_*_v), sizeof, alignof, or a requires-expression.

procedure:
1. List them: `git diff -U0 <base> <head> -- t/ | grep -n -E '^(\\+\\+\\+|@@|\\+.*(STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert))'`; map each '+' line to file:line from the preceding @@ header. For each requires-expression probe used, open its template definition (same file, above the TEST_CASE) and record which functions its body calls.
2. Split by WHAT THE EXPRESSION TOUCHES, not by what is true. BOUNDARY (keep): the expression names a production function declared outside the type under test (a kernel in src/, a free function or member of a different production class) and asks whether the type is accepted or rejected. SHAPE (continue): a type trait, sizeof, alignof, is_constructible/is_convertible/is_default_constructible, or a requires-expression whose body only uses members of the type under test (its ctor, as_view, at, operator[], or their absence). A call to the probed type's own member is SHAPE, not BOUNDARY.
3. For each SHAPE check, find a production static_assert on the same trait: `git grep -n -A3 -E 'static_assert' <head> -- h/ src/ | grep -E '<type>|<alias>'` (resolve aliases, e.g. v_storage = v_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size>, page_size = 64). Same trait on the same type, or on an enclosing type whose sizeof/alignof fixes this one's (kv_block_t contains v_storage), = DUPLICATE; record the header file:line.
4. For each SHAPE check that is not a duplicate, look for a consumer outside the type's own header: grep h/ src/ for uses of the member or trait (`<type>.*\\[`, default construction `<view_type> name;`, `alignof(<type>)`, `assume_aligned`, `_tile_loadd` on a plane pointer). If the comment above the check says "no production code uses/reads this", or cites a review thread or commit as the reason, mark it CONSUMER-LESS without further search. If a consumer exists and no header asserts the trait, mark it MOVE (finding = add the static_assert next to the consumer, not drop the test).
5. Write ONE finding per test block.

discriminating_question: Does the check exercise a production boundary the PR introduces (a production function outside the type, called with the candidate type), or does it describe the shape of a type the PR defines? probe.tightened_rule:
name: Structure-only compile-time checks in tests (boundary probe vs shape of a helper type)

trigger: The diff ADDS, in t/, a STATIC_REQUIRE, STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE or static_assert (compile-time only; runtime REQUIRE/CHECK lines such as is_aligned(), byte comparisons, size() == page_size are out of scope here and belong to the duplicate-coverage rule) whose operand is a type trait (std::is_*_v), sizeof, alignof, or a requires-expression.

procedure:
1. List: git diff -U0 <base> <head> -- t/ | grep -n -E '^(\\+\\+\\+|@@|\\+.*(STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert))'; map each '+' line to file:line at <head> from the preceding @@ header. For each requires-expression template used, open its definition (same file, above the TEST_CASE) and record which functions its body names.
2. Split by WHAT THE EXPRESSION NAMES, not by whether it is true. BOUNDARY (keep, no further steps): the body names a production function declared OUTSIDE the probed type's own header (a kernel in src/, a free function, a member of a different production class) and asks whether the candidate type is accepted or rejected. SHAPE (continue): a type trait, sizeof, alignof, is_constructible / is_convertible / is_default_constructible, or a requires-expression whose body uses only members of the probed type (its constructor, as_view, at, operator[], or their absence, including '= delete' overloads). A call to the probed type's OWN member is SHAPE.
3. For each SHAPE check, find a production static_assert on the same trait: git grep -n -A3 'static_assert' <head> -- h/ src/ | grep -E '<type>|<alias>' (multi-line asserts put the trait on the next line; resolve aliases, e.g. v_storage = v_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size>, page_size = 64). Same trait on the same type, or sizeof/alignof on an enclosing type that contains this one as a member (kv_block_t contains v_storage), = DUPLICATE; record header file:line.
4. For each SHAPE check that is not a duplicate, look for a consumer OUTSIDE the probed type's own header: grep h/ src/ for uses of the member or trait (operator[] on the view, default construction '<view> name;', alignof(<type>), assume_aligned, _tile_loadd on the plane pointer, the implicit-object-creation path in system/memory.hpp). If the comment above the check says 'no production code uses/reads this', or cites a review thread or commit as its reason, mark CONSUMER-LESS without further search. If a consumer exists and no header asserts the trait, mark MOVE (finding = add the static_assert beside the consumer; do not drop the test). Otherwise mark SHAPE-ONLY.
5. Record the source of each check (design table row, PR-body sentence, review thread). A prescription in a design or PR body does NOT exempt it; report 'design-prescribed duplicate' when the design asks for the same trait in a header static_assert and in a test.
6. Write ONE finding per test block: keep the BOUNDARY probes by line range; list the SHAPE checks to drop by kind (no operator[], no view of a temporary, not default-constructible, conversions, sizeof/alignof) and the duplicates with their header file:line; list MOVE items separately.
7. If the PR body counts assertions or cites a check as evidence of a contract, state whether the sentence refers to a BOUNDARY probe or a SHAPE check; count arithmetic over SHAPE checks is a body finding, not a test finding.

discriminating_question (SHAPE checks only; never asked of BOUNDARY probes): Does a production line outside the probed type's own header rely on this trait, and is no header already asserting it? If a header asserts it -> duplicate. If no line relies on it -> shape only. If a line relies on it and no header asserts it -> move the assert into the header.

false_positive_guard: Keep every BOUNDARY probe; 'which line misbehaves if it flipped' does not apply to them (they pin a signature the PR introduces, not behavior). A requires-body that calls the probed type's own member (as_view on a temporary, at() writes) is SHAPE, not BOUNDARY. Keep a sizeof/alignof check only when it pins an ABI consumed outside this repo (hardware descriptor, wire or file format) and no header asserts it. A SHAPE check with a real consumer and no header assert is MOVE, not drop. Pre-existing checks outside the '+' lines are context only. Runtime REQUIRE/CHECK lines (allocator alignment, byte round trips, section size checks) never enter this rule even when they compare against a declared constant. 'The design or PR body asked for it' is not a refutation; only a named production consumer or a missing header static_assert refutes.

The checks at :<c>-<d> only describe the type's shape (test policy: assertions about structure need a consumer): <list by kind>. The <n> trivial-type / size checks at :<e>-<f> repeat <header>:<line> and :<line>. Suggest keeping the probes and dropping the rest.' Add one sentence when the PR body counts assertions or cites a SHAPE check as evidence of a contract.

rule.name: Pairwise overlap of new tests on one production entry point
rule.trigger: A PR adds or widens two or more tests (new TEST_CASE, new SECTION, new GENERATE arm, new TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE instantiation) that drive the same production function, or a single commit answers a gap/omission list with more than one test. Also fires when a comment above a test claims coverage of N branches/cases.
procedure: 1. List the added or widened test units: `git diff <base>..<head> -- 't/*' | grep -n '^+.*\(TEST_CASE\|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\|SECTION(\|GENERATE(\)'`. Also run `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <base>..<head> -- t/` and mark any commit whose message says it closes several gaps/omissions/critic items at once; those tests are the first suspects.

2. For each unit, name the production entry point it drives (the first non-test call after fixture setup, e.g. `dst_book.append(src_book)`) and follow it to the leaf with branches (`git show <head>:h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp`, find copy_token). Enumerate the leaf's branches (each if/else arm, each early return). Map each test input (each GENERATE arm, each token index) to the branch it reaches. Write a table: rows = test units x arms, columns = branches, cell = reached / not reached.

3. For each unit, record what its assertions OBSERVE, not what its setup runs: (a) which output of the branch is compared (copied lane, zeroed partner, return value, counter); (b) against which reference (independent expected data, a formula, or the same object read back = self-consistency); (c) at what precision (bit equality, float equality, NaN absence). A branch counts as covered by a unit only if some assertion of that unit can change outcome when that branch's output is wrong.

4. Pairwise, for every two units whose reached-branch sets intersect: list the (branch, observed output) pairs of each. If unit A's set is a subset of unit B's set, A is duplicate coverage. If the sets differ, name the pairs each one has that the other lacks; that is the finding text (overlap in setup, complementary assertions) and the fix is a merge, not a drop.

5. Compare the comment above each unit with the table from step 3. A claim like 'exercise the four parity combinations' holds only if the unit's assertions observe all four; otherwise flag the comment as describing inputs, not protection.

6. Quote AGENTS.md lines 42-43 and 51-52 (duplicate coverage clauses) in the finding; propose the concrete edit: drop the subset unit, or keep the one arm that reaches an otherwise-unobserved (branch, output) pair and move the rest into the larger unit.
rule.discriminating_question: Is there a deliberate code break that fails test A but passes test B? If every break that fails A also fails B (same branches, B observes everything A observes), A is duplicate coverage. If some break fails only A, the two overlap in setup but protect different outputs.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag as duplicate when the two units observe different outputs of the same branch (copied lane vs zeroed partner; return value vs side effect), compare against different references (independent source data vs read-back of the same object), or run under different build/hardware gates (one behind available() or TRON_CHUNK_SIZE, one not). In those cases report 'overlap in setup, complementary assertions' with a merge suggestion. Do not flag GENERATE arms that are the only NaN-visible or bit-visible check of a branch (here dst_tokens=2 is the only NaN-visible check of the even<-even zeroing branch). Do not flag pre-existing tests the PR merely migrated (API rename only) without new assertions.
rule.finding_template: t/<file>:<line>: `<unit A>` and `<unit B>` (line <N>) both drive `<entry point>` with <inputs>, reaching <branches>. <B> observes <outputs vs reference>, which includes everything <A> observes [or: <A> additionally observes <output> that <B> cannot see because <reason>]. Per AGENTS.md:42-43 (no duplicate coverage without a distinct behavior) drop <A> [or: keep the <arm> of <A> that is the only check of <branch output>, and fold the rest into <B>]; fix the comment at <line> to say what the assertions observe, not what the setup runs.

votes.fix:
Rule name: Pairwise overlap of tests on one production entry point.

Trigger (unchanged in substance): a PR adds or widens two or more test units (TEST_CASE, SECTION, GENERATE arm, TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE instantiation) that reach the same production function, or one commit answers a gap/critic list with more than one test, or a comment above a test claims coverage of N branches/cases, or a new test calls an entry point that an existing test in the same file already calls.

Procedure:
1. List added or widened units: `git diff <base>..<head> -- 't/*' | grep -n '^+.*\(TEST_CASE\|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\|SECTION(\|GENERATE(\)'`. Mark commits whose message closes several gaps at once (`git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <base>..<head> -- t/`); their tests are the first suspects.
2. For each unit name its entry point (first production call after fixture setup, e.g. `dst_book.append(src_book)`). Also collect EXISTING units on the same entry point: `git grep -n '<entry point>' <head> -- t/<same file>`. Existing units are candidate B only; never flag them.
3. Pick the leaf: the function in the PR diff that the entry point reaches (`git diff <base>..<head> --stat` names the files; follow the call chain into them). If the entry point reaches several changed leaves, make one table per leaf. Enumerate the leaf's branches (each if/else arm, each early return) and map each test input (each GENERATE arm, each token index or call) to the branch it reaches.
4. Simulate the writes: for each unit and arm, list in order every write the leaf makes to each output slot (copied lane, zeroed partner, counter, return value). A write is OBSERVABLE only if no later write in the same unit replaces that slot before an assertion reads it. (W5: the bit-exact section zeroes odd slots 3,5,...,63 but each is overwritten by the next odd copy, so it observes no zeroing; the poison section observes only slot 7.)
5. For each unit record what its assertions observe: (a) which observable slot, (b) against which reference (independent expected data, a formula, or the same object read back), (c) at what precision (bits, float, NaN absence), (d) through which read path (production consumer such as scaled_v, or an accessor such as get_v). For each observed (branch, slot) pair apply three fixed breaks and note which the unit catches: wrong copied lane, partner not zeroed or wrong lane, wrong slot offset.
6. Pairwise, for every two units whose branch sets intersect, compare the (branch, slot, read path) sets. A's set a subset of B's -> A is duplicate; report 'drop A'. Sets differ -> report 'overlap in setup, complementary assertions' and name the pairs each has that the other lacks; the fix is to extend the LARGER unit so it observes what the smaller one observes, then drop the smaller one (W5: leave the last odd slot of the bit-exact page unwritten and poisoned, require its bits are 0 for both arms, then drop the GENERATE in the poison section).
7. Compare the comment above each unit with the table. A claim such as 'exercise the four parity combinations' holds only if the assertions observe all four; otherwise report it as a SEPARATE nit (comment describes inputs, not protection).

Discriminating question (unchanged): is there a deliberate break that fails A but passes B? If every break that fails A also fails B, A is duplicate coverage. If some break fails only A, the two overlap in setup but protect different outputs.

False-positive guard: do not call A a duplicate when A observes a slot B cannot see (because B overwrites it, step 4), compares against a different reference (independent data vs read-back of the same object), reads through a different production path (scaled_v vs get_v), uses a different precision (bits vs float vs NaN absence), or runs under a different build/hardware gate (available(), TRON_CHUNK_SIZE). In those cases report the complementary variant with the merge direction of step 6. Do not flag pre-existing units the PR only migrated (API rename, no new assertion).

Finding template (one ask; cite the policy by its clause, not a line number):
`t/<file>:<line>: this <unit A> and <unit B> (line <N>) both run <inputs> through <entry point>, reaching <branches>. <B> already checks <what B observes, vs which reference, via which read path>; this one adds only <nothing | the one (branch, slot) pair A alone observes, and why B cannot see it>. The test policy rules out duplicate coverage that protects no distinct behavior: <drop this one | extend <B> to <concrete change that makes B observe A's slot> and drop this one>.`
Second, separate nit when step 7 fires: `Nit: the comment at <line> says <claim>; the assertions here can only see <observed slots>.`

probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Same experiment run twice on one production entry point.

Trigger (all four must hold): (1) the PR adds or widens two test units (TEST_CASE, SECTION, GENERATE arm, TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE instantiation), or one new unit plus one unit it widens; (2) both call the same production entry point as the operation under test (the first production call after the unit's own writes, e.g. `dst_book.append(src_book)`), not merely share a fixture that a TEST_CASE fills once for all its sections; (3) both feed that call the same input shape, judged by the text: the same GENERATE list or the same named constants, the same token or size set, the same source value type; (4) both reach the same set of leaf branches in the function the PR diff changed. A commit message that says it closes several gaps or critic items at once raises the priority of its units but is not by itself a trigger. A comment that claims coverage of N cases is a separate nit, not a trigger.

Procedure (unchanged steps 1-5 of the rule-lens fix: list units, name entry points and existing callers, pick the changed leaf, simulate the write order so a slot counts as observed only if no later write in the same unit replaces it before an assertion, record for each unit the observed (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) set). Step 6 replaced: compare the two sets only for the pair that passed the trigger. If A's set is a subset of B's, report 'duplicate coverage, drop A'. If A adds observations B lacks, report ONE finding at A: 'same experiment as B; A alone observes <pair>; give B that observation by <one concrete edit> and drop A'. Never report a pair whose setups differ as 'complementary'; at most mention it in one line without a fix.

Guard (any one suppresses the finding): the two units feed the entry point different source value types (a different `if constexpr` arm in the leaf, e.g. bf16 vs fp16 vs float rows) or different token or size sets; they call different entry points even if those share a helper (at() vs get_v, append_v_row vs copy_token, both using pair_base); one of them is pre-existing and the PR changed only its API spelling; they run under different build or hardware gates (then the finding is the gate, not the overlap); the smaller unit is the only NaN-visible or bit-visible observation of a branch output and the larger unit cannot absorb it with a local edit. A shared fill loop before the sections, a shared read-back helper, or a shared named constant is not shared setup unless the operation under test is also the same.

Discriminating question kept: is there a deliberate break that fails A but passes B? If none, A is duplicate. If some, name it and give B that observation before dropping A.

Finding template (one ask): `t/<file>:<line>: this <unit A> and <unit B> (line <N>) run the same <inputs> through <entry point>, reaching <branches>. <B> already checks <what, vs which reference, via which read path>; this one adds only <nothing | the (branch, slot) pair B cannot see because B overwrites it>. The test policy rules out duplicate coverage that protects no distinct behavior: <drop this one | extend B by <concrete edit> and drop this one>.` Comment-vs-assertion mismatches go in a separate nit.

rule.name: Test name states the enforced contract
rule.trigger: A diff adds or edits lines inside a Catch2 TEST_CASE or SECTION (or a gtest TEST / a test function) without changing the name string, OR changes a comment inside a test from one verb to its opposite (preserve/zero, keep/drop, accept/reject, allow/throw), OR a review or commit message refers to a test by its name while describing behavior.
procedure: List every test hunk: git -C <wt> diff <base>..<head> -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' 't/*.hpp' | grep -n '^@@' and note file + new-side line of each hunk.

For each hunk, find the enclosing names: git -C <wt> show <head>:<file> | awk -v L=<hunk line> 'NR<=L && /TEST_CASE\(|SECTION\(|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\(|^TEST\(/ {name=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "name}' (repeat for the nearest TEST_CASE and the nearest SECTION above the hunk).
Extract the claim verb and object from each name string: the verb (preserves, zeroes, keeps, rejects, matches, propagates, ...) and its object (poison, bits, partner, NaN ...).

Read the assertions of that test or section: git -C <wt> show <head>:<file> | sed -n '<section start>,<section end>p' | grep -n 'REQUIRE\|CHECK\|STATIC_REQUIRE\|THROWS'. Write one sentence per assertion: 'fails when <state>'.

Compare: does the name's verb describe the state that makes the assertion FAIL (bad) or PASS (good)? The name must describe the passing state. Example: name 'preserves poison', assertion REQUIRE_FALSE(isnan(...)) fails when the poison is preserved -> mismatch.

Also compare the name against every comment in the same test that was changed in the diff (git diff <base>..<head> -- <file> | grep '^[-+] *//'): if a comment verb flipped (will preserve -> must zero) and the name kept the old verb, flag.

Check the test-case header comment and the commit messages for the same stale name: git -C <wt> log --format=%B <base>..<head> | grep -n '<name string>' and grep -n '<name string>' <file>. Every occurrence must be fixed together with the rename.
Check the PR body and any review response that cites the test by name: a sentence of the form 'X is covered by test "<name>"' must be re-read with the corrected name.
rule.discriminating_question: If I read only the name string and the REQUIRE lines of this test, does the name describe the state in which the assertions PASS? If the name describes the state in which they FAIL, or a state the assertions never observe, the name is wrong.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag a name that is a topic label rather than a claim (e.g. 'scaled_v padding NaN', 'book.append()'); only a name with a verb that asserts behavior can contradict an assertion. Do not flag a name that was wrong on main AND whose section the diff did not touch (out of scope; mention once as pre-existing at most). Do not flag when the name describes a precondition the test sets up (e.g. 'with poisoned padding') rather than the outcome. Do not propose renames that only reword a correct name.
rule.finding_template: t/<file>:<line>: SECTION "<name>" says <name verb+object>, but its assertions pass only when <opposite state> (REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan(...)) at :<line>; the comment at :<line> now says '<new comment verb>'). Rename the section to "<verb that matches the passing state>" and update the <N> other places that quote the old name (<file:line>, commit message, PR body).

votes.fix:
name: Test name states the enforced contract

trigger (any one):
  (a) a diff adds or edits lines inside a Catch2 TEST_CASE/SECTION/TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE (or gtest TEST) body and leaves the name string unchanged;
  (b) a diff changes a comment inside a test body from one verb to its opposite (preserve/zero, keep/drop, accept/reject, allow/throw, propagate/block) while the enclosing name keeps the old verb;
  (c) a commit message, PR body or review text quotes a test name AND the same sentence states a behavior whose verb is the opposite of the name's verb.

procedure:
  1. List test hunks: git -C <wt> diff <base>..<head> -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' 't/*.hpp' | grep -n '^+++\|^@@'. Note file + new-side start line per hunk.
  2. Find the enclosing names with an indent bound (the plain 'last match above' awk misattributes hunks that follow a closed sibling section): git -C <wt> show <head>:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /^TEST_CASE\(|^TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\(|^TEST\(/ {tc=NR": "$0} NR<=L && /^  SECTION\(/ {sec=NR": "$0} NR<=L && /^  }$/ {sec=""} END{print tc; print sec}'. If the hunk is a NEW test or section, skip it here and judge its new name in step 5 as well.
  3. Section end: the first line matching `^  }$` after the SECTION line (first `^}$` after a TEST_CASE line). Print the body: sed -n '<start>,<end>p'.
  4. From each name string write the claim: subject, verb, object (append_v / preserves / poison). A name with no behavior verb (a topic label, 'scaled_v padding NaN'; a stimulus, 'append under poison'; a regression label naming the defect, 'NaN leak from padding slot') has no claim: stop for that name.
  5. For every REQUIRE/CHECK/STATIC_REQUIRE/REQUIRE_THROWS/REQUIRE_NOTHROW in the body that observes the name's object, write one line: 'fails when <state>'. Then answer: does the name's verb describe the state in which these lines PASS? If it describes the state in which they FAIL, or a state no assertion observes, the name is wrong.
  6. Compare the name with the test's own comments in the diff: git -C <wt> diff <base>..<head> -- <file> | grep '^[-+] *//' | grep -i '<name verb>\|<opposite verb>'. A removed line with the name's verb plus an added line with the opposite verb is a flip: flag even if the assertions are unchanged.
  7. Collect the other sites that quote the old name in the PR's own text: grep -n '<name string>' <file> (header comments) and the PR body. Commit messages are not an ask (they are gone at squash); mention them only if the PR is not being squashed.

discriminating question:
  Reading only the name string, the REQUIRE lines, and the comments the diff touched inside this test: does the name's verb describe the state in which the assertions pass, and does it agree with the verb the test's own comments now use? 'preserves poison' + REQUIRE_FALSE(isnan(...)) + comment 'must zero this NaN' fails both halves.

false-positive guard:
  - No behavior verb in the name (topic, stimulus, or regression label that names the defect in noun form): not a claim, do not flag.
  - The verb describes a state the TEST'S OWN CODE establishes before the call under test ('with poisoned padding'): not a claim about the code under test, do not flag. A verb attributed to the code under test ('append_v preserves ...') is a claim even if it reads like setup.
  - The name was already wrong on <base> AND the diff does not touch the body of that test or section: out of scope, one line 'pre-existing' at most.
  - The name is correct but could be worded better: do not propose a rename.

probe.tightened_rule:
name: Test name states the enforced contract

trigger (any one; a hunk that only re-spells a call's arguments, with no added or removed REQUIRE/CHECK/STATIC_REQUIRE line and no changed '//' line, is an API migration and does NOT trigger):
  (a) the diff adds, removes or rewrites an assertion, or a comment, or the stimulus (the values the test writes before the call under test) inside a Catch2 TEST_CASE/SECTION/TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE (or gtest TEST) body, and the enclosing name string is unchanged in the diff;
  (b) the diff changes a comment inside a test body from one verb to its opposite (preserve/zero, keep/drop, accept/reject, allow/throw, propagate/block) and the enclosing name keeps the old verb;
  (c) a PR body, review reply or (only if the PR will not be squashed) commit message quotes a test name AND the same sentence states a behavior whose verb is the opposite of the name's verb.

procedure:
  1. List test hunks: git -C <wt> diff <base>..<head> -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' 't/*.hpp' | grep -n '^+++\|^@@'. Drop hunks that are pure call re-spellings (see trigger).
  2. For each remaining hunk, if its added lines contain TEST_CASE(/SECTION(/TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE(/TEST(, those are the units to judge (a new unit). Otherwise find the enclosing unit with the indent-bound awk: git -C <wt> show <head>:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /^TEST_CASE\(|^TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\(|^TEST\(/ {tc=NR": "$0} NR<=L && /^  SECTION\(/ {sec=NR": "$0} NR<=L && /^  }$/ {sec=""} END{print tc; print sec}'. Multi-line names: take the next line when the macro line ends in '('.
  3. Judge the SMALLEST enclosing unit only (the SECTION when there is one). A TEST_CASE name that has SECTIONs is a summary; judge it only against assertions outside every SECTION.
  4. Unit end: first '^  }$' after a SECTION line, first '^}$' after a TEST_CASE line. Read the body.
  5. From the name write subject / verb / object (append_v / preserves / poison). No behavior verb (topic label 'scaled_v padding NaN', stimulus 'single-token dirty-buffer reuse', regression label naming the defect as a noun 'NaN leak from padding slot'): no claim, stop.
  6. For every REQUIRE/CHECK/STATIC_REQUIRE/REQUIRE_THROWS/REQUIRE_NOTHROW in the body that observes the name's OBJECT, write 'fails when <state>'. Read the setup lines that put that object into its pre-call state (the lines between the unit start and the call under test) so that 'preserves X' is judged against what X was before the call. Answer: does the name's verb describe the state in which these assertions PASS? If it describes the state in which they FAIL, the name is wrong. An assertion that observes something the name does not mention is not a mismatch (name scope, not contradiction): do not flag it under this rule.
  7. Comment flip check: git -C <wt> diff <base>..<head> -- <file> | grep '^[-+] *//' restricted to the unit's line range. A removed line carrying the name's verb plus an added line carrying its opposite is a flip: flag even if the assertions are unchanged. A new unit has no removed lines, so this step never fires on a new unit.
  8. Collect the other sites that quote the old name: grep -n '<name string>' <file> (header comments) and the PR body. Commit messages only if the PR is not being squashed.

discriminating question:
  Reading the name string, the setup of the name's object, the assertions on that object, and the comments the diff touched inside this unit: does the name's verb describe the state in which those assertions pass, and does it agree with the verb the unit's own comments now use? 'append_v preserves poison' + REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan(actual_v[i])) + comment 'must zero this NaN' fails both halves.

false-positive guard:
  - Hunk is a pure call re-spelling (argument wrapper, formatting, named constant for the same value): no trigger; do not read the unit.
  - No behavior verb in the name: not a claim, do not flag.
  - The verb describes a state the TEST'S OWN CODE establishes before the call under test ('with poisoned padding'): not a claim about the code under test, do not flag. A verb attributed to the code under test ('append_v preserves ...') is a claim.
  - 'preserves / keeps X' is judged against X's pre-call state from the setup lines; an assertion that X is still absent, incomplete or zero after the call is a PASS state for 'preserves' when the setup left X absent, incomplete or zero (the heterogeneous append case: slot 1 never V-completed in setup, REQUIRE_FALSE(is_kv_complete(slot 1)) is preservation).
  - A TEST_CASE name is judged only against assertions outside its SECTIONs; a SECTION whose own name states a conversion ('truncate', 'convert', 'round') does not contradict a TEST_CASE summary verb ('keep their bits').
  - An assertion the name does not mention is out of this rule's scope (report it, if at all, under a 'name does not cover new assertion' note, never as 'name says the opposite').
  - The name was already wrong on <base> AND the diff does not touch the body of that unit: out of scope; at most one line 'pre-existing'. A header comment quoting the old name that is unchanged from <base> is listed as a rename site, not as a second defect.
  - A correct name that could be worded better: do not propose a rename.

finding template (one sentence, Wade register):
  'Nit: t/<file>:<line>: the section is still named "<name>", but <what the assertions now require, quoting the REQUIRE at :<line>; the comment at :<line> now says "<new verb phrase>">. Rename it to "<verb matching the passing state> <object>"; the header comment at :<line> and the PR body quote the old name too.'
  Example: 'Nit: t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3293: the section is still named "append_v preserves poison", but it now asserts the poison is zeroed (REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan(actual_v[i])) at :3385; the comment at :3325 says "must zero this NaN"). Rename it to "append_v zeroes the poisoned partner"; the header comment at :3276 quotes the old name too.'

scope note: the same instinct (a name or doc claim checked against the code that enforces it) covers function and variable names in the Wade corpus; keep this rule on test names and add a sibling rule for renamed or re-bodied functions whose verb no longer matches.
