rule.name: Out-of-scope shared-header hunk needs an owner sign-off
rule.trigger: Any of: (a) the diff touches a file outside the directories the PR title or Short version names; (b) a hunk adds a symbol at global namespace (operator new/delete overload, free function, macro, inline variable) or edits a header under h/system, h/pos, h/common, h/tron/hardware; (c) a comment, Note or commit message in the diff says a revert is undetectable ('no test fails if', 'nothing can catch', 'cannot be tested', 'tests behave the same either way').
procedure: 1. List touched files: `git diff --stat BASE..HEAD`. Read the PR title and Short version; mark each file in-scope or out-of-scope by directory.

2. For each out-of-scope file and each header, compute fan-out: `git grep -l '<path from h/>' HEAD -- h src t bin | wc -l` for direct includers, then a transitive closure over `#include` lines of all .hpp/.cpp at HEAD (script: parse includes, reverse map, BFS from the file). Record 'N direct, M transitive of T files'. Treat M >= 50 or any header under h/system, h/pos, h/common, h/tron/hardware as shared.

3. Find global-namespace additions: `git diff BASE..HEAD -- <file> | grep -n -E '^\+.*(operator new|operator delete|#define|using namespace)'`, and for each added function check with `git show HEAD:<file> | awk 'NR<=L'` whether the nearest preceding `namespace` line is a close (`}  // namespace`) rather than an open.

4. Find untestable claims: `git log -p BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E 'no test (fails|can)|nothing can catch|cannot be tested|not testable|behave the same either way'`. For each hit, list the tests that touch the function (`git grep -n '<function>' HEAD -- t/`) and state what each asserts; if none asserts the mechanism, record 'revert undetected'.

5. Provenance: `git log --format='%h %an %aI %s' BASE..HEAD -- <file>`. For the commit that introduced the hunk, find its origin: `gh pr list --state all --search <sha>` or the PR body's commit table; record whether it was a separate draft PR, a fast-forward fold, or a maintainer-authored PR. Compare with the PR body: does the body say where the hunk came from?

6. Ownership: `git log --format=%an BASE -- <file> | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3` gives the owners. Then `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.path=="<file>") | [.user.login, .created_at, .body] | @tsv'`. Classify each owner comment as 'mechanism accepted' (names the approach and says it is fine, agree, LGTM, go ahead) or 'wording/clarification only'.

7. Check dates: the sign-off comment must postdate the introducing commit. A reply that cites a commit as 'the response to the owner' is wrong when `git show -s --format=%aI <commit>` is earlier than the owner's comment.
8. Emit a finding when (shared or out-of-scope file, or global-namespace symbol) AND (revert undetected OR owner not among the hunk's authors) AND (no owner comment classified 'mechanism accepted').
rule.discriminating_question: Can a reader of this PR's conversation find a sentence by an owner of the touched file that accepts the mechanism (not the wording), and would at least one test fail if the mechanism were reverted? If either answer is no, it is a defect of the PR's review state.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag when the owner authored the hunk (for example #4697 and #4698 are Ben's own PRs merged into the branch). Do not flag an in-scope file of a PR the owner approved after the hunk landed; the approval covers it. Do not flag when a test fails on revert, even in a shared header; then the change is ordinary code under review. Do not flag comment-only hunks in shared headers. Do not demand a sign-off for a global symbol that is private to a .cpp file.

votes.fix:
Name: Global symbol or shared-header hunk whose correctness no test observes needs a named owner's acceptance.

Trigger (any one): (b) a hunk adds or changes a symbol at global namespace in any header (operator new/delete overload, free function, macro, inline variable), or adds non-comment lines to a header under h/system, h/pos, h/common or h/tron/hardware; (c) a comment, Note or commit message says a revert is undetectable ('no test fails if', 'nothing can catch', 'cannot be tested', 'behave the same either way'). Do not use 'out-of-scope by directory' as a trigger; it belongs to the sibling 'unrelated changes' rule, and here the PR body names memory.hpp as a deliberate change.

Procedure:
1. Global-namespace definitions: `git diff BASE..HEAD -- '*.hpp' | grep -n -E '^\+(TRON\(|[a-zA-Z_].*\b)(operator (new|delete)|#define|using namespace)'`; drop lines starting with `+//` and lines containing `::operator` (calls). For each remaining hit, `git show HEAD:<file> | awk 'NR<=L && /namespace/' | tail -1` must be a close (`}  // namespace`) for the symbol to count as global.
2. Untestable claims: `git grep -n -i -E 'no test (fails|can)|nothing can catch|cannot be tested|not testable|behave the same either way' HEAD -- h src t` and `git log --format='%h %B' BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E <same>`. For each hit, list tests that call the function (`git grep -n '<function>' HEAD -- t/`) and state what each asserts. Record 'revert undetected' when none asserts the route or mechanism.
3. Fan-out (reported in the finding, not a trigger): direct includers `git grep -l '<path from h/>' HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | wc -l`; transitive closure script over #include lines of all .hpp/.cpp/.h/.cc/.inl at HEAD; report 'N direct, M transitive of T source files'.
4. Provenance: `git log --format='%h %an %aI %s' BASE..HEAD -- <file>`; for the introducing commit, `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls` and take the earliest PR that is not the PR under review; record draft PR, fast-forward fold, or owner-authored PR. Check whether the PR body's commit table names that origin.
5. Owners (a set, in this order): CODEOWNERS entry for the path when the file exists; else the three most recent distinct authors of the file at BASE (`git log --format=%an BASE -- <file> | awk '!s[$0]++' | head -3`) plus any requested reviewer of the PR who authored a commit to the file. Do not rank by commit count: on memory.hpp that ranking puts the maintainer last.
6. Acceptance: `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.path=="<file>") | [.user.login,.created_at,.in_reply_to_id,.body] | @tsv'` plus `.../pulls/<N>/reviews`. Classify each owner comment as 'mechanism accepted' (names the approach and says agree, fine, LGTM, go ahead) or 'wording/clarification only'. An APPROVED review by an owner dated after the introducing commit counts as acceptance for every file.
7. Dates: acceptance must postdate the introducing commit (`git show -s --format=%aI <sha>`). A reply that cites a commit older than the owner's comment as 'the response to the owner' is wrong; say so.
8. Emit when (global-namespace definition OR non-comment hunk in the listed directories) AND (revert undetected: step 2 found no test asserting the mechanism) AND (no owner acceptance after the introducing commit).

Discriminating question: Does the correctness of this hunk rest on a guarantee that no test in the repo observes (a standard-wording rule such as [intro.object], an allocator route, an ODR or ABI property), and has an owner of the file written a sentence that accepts that mechanism, not only the wording? Defect when the first answer is yes and the second is no.

False-positive guards: skip when the hunk's author is in the owner set; skip when an owner APPROVED the PR after the hunk landed; skip comment-only hunks; skip when a test asserts the mechanism (then step 8 cannot fire by construction); skip a global symbol private to one .cpp file; skip ordinary behavior-preserving refactors in in-scope headers (kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp here) even when their transitive fan-out exceeds 50, because fan-out is a report number, not a trigger.

The header reaches 153 of 502 .hpp/.cpp files (42 direct). probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Global symbol or shared-system-header hunk whose correctness no test observes needs a named owner's acceptance of the placement.

Trigger (BOTH halves must hold; neither alone fires):
(1) Placement half: a hunk adds or changes a definition at global namespace in any header (operator new/delete overload, free function, macro, inline variable; verified by the namespace-close check, after dropping lines that start with `+//` and lines that contain `::operator`, which are calls), OR adds non-comment lines to a header under h/system, h/pos, h/common or h/tron/hardware. Symbols inside a named namespace in a header under h/tron/tensor, h/tron/models, h/tron/kernels or h/tron/scheduler do not satisfy this half, whatever their fan-out.
(2) Unobserved-guarantee half: the correctness of the hunk rests on a guarantee no test observes. Evidence is either (i) a sentence in the hunk's own comment at HEAD or in its introducing commit message that says a revert is undetectable ('no test fails if', 'nothing can catch', 'cannot be tested', 'behave the same either way', 'no test can tell'), grep restricted to the touched files at HEAD plus `git log --format='%h %B' BASE..HEAD`, never the whole tree; or (ii) step 'tests' below finds no test under t/ that asserts the mechanism (the allocation route, the object creation, the ODR or ABI property), only its by-products (non-null, alignment, size).
Optional strengthener (never a trigger by itself): the hunk arrived by a fold (fast-forward, squash or merge) of a stacked or draft PR, or a design record for the PR holds an unresolved 'ask the owner' item. Then the finding also says the fold bypassed its own gate.

Removed from the trigger: 'out-of-scope by directory' (belongs to the sibling 'unrelated changes' rule, with the remedy 'split it out'), and 'transitive includers >= 50' (fan-out is a number reported in the finding, not a trigger; six of this PR's eight headers exceed 50).

Procedure:
1. Global definitions: `git diff BASE..HEAD -- '*.hpp' | grep -n -E '^\+.*(operator (new|delete)|#define|using namespace|^\+(inline|constexpr|static|template|void|auto|[A-Za-z_:<>]+\*?) [^;]*\(.*\)\s*(noexcept)?\s*\{?$)' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+\s*//' | grep -v '::operator'`. For each hit at line L of file F: `git show HEAD:F | awk 'NR<=L && /namespace/' | tail -1` must be a close (`}  // namespace`) for the symbol to be global. Also list headers under h/system, h/pos, h/common, h/tron/hardware with non-comment added lines.
2. Untestable sentence: `git diff BASE..HEAD --name-only | xargs -I{} git grep -n -i -E 'no test (fails|can)|nothing can catch|cannot be tested|not testable|behave the same either way' HEAD -- {}` plus `git log --format='%h %B' BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E <same>`. Record each hit once per sentence, not once per reword commit.
3. Tests: for the function or symbol in the hunk, `git grep -n '<symbol>' HEAD -- t/`. For each test, state the asserted property. Record 'revert undetected' when no assertion fails if the mechanism is reverted (here: t/t_heap_v2.cpp:1206-1220 asserts non-null and 64-byte alignment; a revert to dma_allocate_aligned passes both).
4. Fan-out (report only): direct = `git grep -l -E '^\s*#\s*include.*<path from h/>' HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | wc -l`; transitive = closure over #include lines of all .hpp/.cpp/.h/.cc/.inl at HEAD (rule-m1/fanout.py); write 'N direct, M transitive of T source files'. Measuring callers of a changed function is not a substitute when the hunk adds a symbol to a header.
5. Provenance: `git log --format='%h %an %aI %s' BASE..HEAD -- <file>`; for the introducing commit, `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls` and take the earliest PR that is not the PR under review; record draft PR, fast-forward fold, or owner-authored PR. Check whether the PR body's commit table names that origin. If a design record or memory note for the hunk names a question for the owner, search the PR comments for it; an unposted gate is recorded in the finding.
6. Owners (a set, never a commit-count ranking): the CODEOWNERS entry for the path when the file exists; else the three most recent distinct authors of the file at BASE (`git log --format=%an BASE -- <file> | awk '!s[$0]++' | head -3`) plus every requested reviewer of the PR who has a commit on the file at BASE. For a new file the owner set is the owners of its directory's other headers. On h/system/memory.hpp this gives Ben Gamari, rbjarnason-positron, Brian Hamon.
7. Acceptance: `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.path=="<file>") | [.user.login,.created_at,.in_reply_to_id,.body] | @tsv'` and `.../pulls/<N>/reviews`. A comment counts as 'placement accepted' only when (a) its author is in the owner set, (b) its date is after the introducing commit (`git show -s --format=%aI <sha>`), and (c) it names the added symbol or its placement (the global overload, the header it lives in) and says keep, fine, agree, LGTM or go ahead. Agreement with the diagnosis ('the old code was incorrect', 'rightly playing language lawyer'), a reword or clarification request, and 'seems useful' are not acceptance. Test for (c): would the sentence still be true if the symbol were moved out of the shared header? If yes, it accepts the problem, not the placement. An APPROVED review by an owner dated after the introducing commit counts for every file of the PR. A reply that cites a commit older than the owner's comment as the response to it is wrong; say so with both dates.
8. Emit one finding per mechanism when (trigger half 1) AND (trigger half 2) AND (no placement acceptance). Fold the consumer-side hunks of the same mechanism (here the std::launder accessors in kv_cache.hpp) into that one finding as a sentence, not as a second finding.

Discriminating question: Does this hunk put a symbol at global namespace or into a system-wide header, AND does its correctness rest on a guarantee that no test in the repo observes, AND has an owner of the file written, after the hunk landed, a sentence that accepts that placement rather than the problem it solves? Defect when the first two answers are yes and the third is no.

False-positive guards: skip when the hunk's author is in the owner set (so Ben's #4697 and #4698 commits skip even in files where he has no commit by count); skip when an owner APPROVED the PR after the hunk landed; skip comment-only hunks; skip when a test under t/ asserts the mechanism; skip a global symbol private to one .cpp file; never flag a test file or an in-scope header (h/tron/models, h/tron/tensor, h/tron/kernels, h/tron/scheduler) on ownership or fan-out alone, even above 50 transitive includers; never demand a sign-off as the remedy for an unrelated hunk (that remedy is 'split it out', from the sibling rule).

rule.name: hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated-change detector)
rule.trigger: Any PR with more than one commit, or any diff hunk whose added lines contain none of the identifiers the PR introduces, or any commit subject of the form 'Name/Rename/Brace/Clean up/Shorten ...' in a PR whose title is a feature or type change. Also when a draft PR was folded into the reviewed PR (memory notes say 'folded', 'stacked', 'fast-forward').
procedure: 1. List the branch commits: `git log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD` (BASE = the main side of the last merge, e.g. e5fa372c19; HEAD = the reviewed head). Write down the PR title and the 'What changes' bullets of the PR body as reviewed.

2. For each commit subject, ask: does it name a type, function, Note or behavior listed in the PR title or 'What changes'? Mark subjects that name only a rename, a naming pass, braces, comment wording or a test addition (here: 'Name the AMX tile numbers in the attention kernels').

3. Build the PR's identifier set: new headers' public names plus names in 'What changes' (here: v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, native_k_view, const_native_k_view, v_packed, copy_token, append_v_row, load_row, dma_allocation, dma_allocation_t, launder, V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64). Command: `git diff BASE..HEAD -- h/ | grep -o '^+.*\b\(struct\|class\|using\|constexpr\|inline\) [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*' | sort -u`.

4. For each file in `git diff --stat BASE..HEAD`, split the diff into hunks (`git diff BASE..HEAD -- FILE`). For each hunk collect its '+' lines and grep them for the identifier set. A hunk with zero hits is a candidate.

5. For each candidate hunk, find the commit that added it: `git log --format='%h %s' BASE..HEAD -- FILE` and `git show <commit> -- FILE`. If that commit is one marked in step 2, the hunk is unrelated unless step 6 clears it.

6. Clearance checks (any one clears the hunk): (a) the PR's functional change rewrites the same statement (e.g. `k_page` -> `k_rows` on that line); (b) a review thread of THIS PR asked for it (quote the thread id); (c) the PR body claims it in a sentence a reader can find (`grep -n -i '<file basename>\|<constant name>' body.md`). Here body:52 says 'The tile loads are unchanged' - the opposite of a claim.

7. For a test hunk: identify the contract the new assertion pins and check whether it exists at BASE: `git show BASE:<header> | grep -n <contract keyword>` (here `alloc_align` at memory.hpp:146). If the contract pre-dates the PR and the assertion references no PR identifier, the test belongs on main or with the change that owns the contract, not in this PR.

8. Report each remaining hunk with: file:lines at HEAD, the commit id, the one-line reason it is not needed by the PR, and the body sentence (if any) it contradicts. Recommend 'split out' (own PR) or 'drop'. Count the commits and say if the history should be squashed into topical commits.
rule.discriminating_question: If this hunk alone were reverted, would any sentence in the PR body stop being true, or would any symbol the PR introduces stop compiling or stop being tested? If no, the hunk is an unrelated change.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag: a rename forced by a signature or type change on the same line (the typed view's `k_page` -> `k_rows`); naming or bracing on lines the PR itself added (the guide check's 'PR-added lines only' rule); a change a reviewer of this PR asked for in a thread (cite it); a cleanup the PR title or 'What changes' lists as bundled and that the maintainer already accepted; a test that pins a contract the PR creates or changes (e.g. a check that the new operator new[] wrapper forwards alignment would be in scope if the PR body claimed that forwarding - it does not). A commit on main's lines is not automatically unrelated; the test is whether a PR claim needs it.
rule.finding_template: <file>:<lines at HEAD> (commit <id>, '<subject>') changes lines the PR's <feature> did not need to touch: <what it does, e.g. replaces 26 tile-number literals with 14 named constants / adds an is_aligned CHECK for a contract that exists at BASE memory.hpp:146>. The PR body <does not mention it | says '<contradicting sentence>'>. Not part of <PR title>; move it to its own PR (or drop it) and squash the remaining commits into topical ones.

rule.name: "hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated-change detector)"

rule.trigger: "Always, for every PR review; the cost is one `git log`. Highest priority when a memory note or the PR thread says a draft PR was folded, stacked or fast-forwarded into this one, or when any commit subject starts with Name/Rename/Brace/Clean up/Shorten/Clarify/Reword."

rule.procedure:
1. BASE = the main side of the last merge into the branch (`git merge-base` or the first parent of the merge commit; here e5fa372c19). HEAD = the reviewed head (96a6220ab6). Save the PR title and the 'What changes' bullets of the body as reviewed.
2. `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short --no-merges BASE..HEAD`. Mark each commit MAIN-FEATURE (subject names a type, function, Note or behavior in the title or 'What changes') or SIDE (subject names only a rename, naming pass, braces, comment wording, or a test addition). Here: ec795fbce8 'Name the AMX tile numbers in the attention kernels' = SIDE; 39a6899446 = MAIN-FEATURE (DMA allocation) but it is the folded draft #4587, so treat its hunks outside memory.hpp/kv_cache.hpp as SIDE.
3. Write the PR identifier set BY HAND from the title, 'What changes' and the new headers (here: v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, native_k_view, const_native_k_view, v_packed, copy_token, append_v_row, load_row, dma_allocation, dma_allocation_t, launder, V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64). Confirm each name with `git diff BASE..HEAD | grep -c '\\b<name>\\b'`; do not derive the set from a keyword grep (a struct/class/using grep misses functions and members, and the `^+.*` form truncates names under grep -o).
4. Write the PR rename map: pairs where the PR replaced one symbol with another on existing lines (here k_page -> k_rows, v_page -> v_pairs, dma_allocate_aligned -> ::operator new[]).
5. For each SIDE commit: `git show <commit> --stat`, then per file `git show <commit> -- FILE`. For each hunk, count its '-' lines that exist verbatim in `git show BASE:FILE` (`grep -cF`). A hunk is a CANDIDATE when (a) at least half of its '-' lines exist verbatim at BASE and (b) its '+' lines contain no name from step 3. (Hunks with zero '-' lines at BASE are polish of PR-added lines: in scope, skip.) Do not scan the whole diff hunk by hunk: on this PR 56 of 83 hunks have no PR identifier, so that filter alone does not narrow.
6. Clearance, token level: for each '-'/'+' pair in a candidate hunk, apply the step-4 rename map to the '-' line; if the result equals the '+' line, the pair is forced by the PR and cleared. A pair where another token also changed (`4 /* dest tile */` -> `K_EVEN_BLOCK_TILE_4` on a line whose continuation got k_page -> k_rows) is NOT cleared. Also cleared: a hunk a review thread of THIS PR asked for (quote the thread id), or a hunk the body claims in a sentence a reader can find (`grep -n -i '<file basename>\\|<constant name>' body.md`).
7. Revert test for each remaining hunk: apply `git show <commit> -- FILE` in reverse onto `git show HEAD:FILE` in the scratchpad (`patch -R`). Record: does any body sentence stop being true; does any step-3 name stop compiling or stop being tested; by how many lines does `diff BASE:FILE reverted` shrink. Here: body:52 'The tile loads are unchanged' becomes true, nothing stops compiling, the file's diff against BASE drops from 126 to 38 lines.
8. Test hunks (new CHECK/REQUIRE/STATIC_REQUIRE): name the callee the assertion exercises. If the callee is NOT in `git diff BASE..HEAD` and the assertion uses no step-3 name, the test is unrelated (report as in step 9). If the callee IS rewritten by the PR (here try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite: `dma_allocate_aligned(...)` -> `::operator new[](..., dma_allocation, alignment)`), the test is a regression guard for the PR; report it only as a BODY GAP ('the body never says the new operator new[] wrapper preserves alignment; add the sentence or move the check with the DMA change'), never as unrelated.
9. Report each remaining hunk as one finding with one ask (template below). Report the commit count and the squash request as a SEPARATE finding.

rule.discriminating_question: "Two tests, both must hold: (1) this hunk changes lines that exist verbatim at BASE (at least half of its '-' lines), and (2) reverting this hunk alone leaves every PR body sentence true and every symbol the PR introduces compiling and tested. A hunk that fails (1) is polish of the PR's own lines (in scope). A hunk that fails (2) is needed. A hunk that passes both is an unrelated change."

rule.false_positive_guard: "Do not flag: a '-'/'+' pair that differs only by the PR's rename map (k_page -> k_rows); any change on lines that do not exist at BASE (new headers, new Notes, new tests: the naming passes 1c87d66926 and 5051264d80, the Note [KV block lifetime] rewordings, 2280e4beb2); a change a reviewer of THIS PR asked for (cite the thread); a change the PR title or 'What changes' lists as bundled and that a maintainer accepted in a thread; a test whose callee the PR rewrote (that is a regression guard; at most a body-gap finding). A change on main's lines is not automatically unrelated: the test is whether a body sentence or a PR symbol needs it."

rule.finding_template (one ask per finding): "<file>:<lines at HEAD> (commit <id>, '<subject>') changes <N> lines that exist at BASE and that <PR feature> does not touch: <what it does, e.g. replaces 26 tile-number literals with 14 named constants>. Reverting it alone keeps the body true (body:<line> even says '<sentence>') and nothing the PR introduces stops compiling. Not part of <PR title>: please split it into its own PR." Separate finding for history: "<N> commits, <M> of them rewording one Note; please squash into topical commits." Separate finding for a test body gap: "<test file>:<line> CHECK(<assertion>) pins <contract> of <callee>, which this PR rewrites (<file>:<line>); the body never claims it. Add the sentence or move the check with the <feature> change."

probe.tightened_rule: name: hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated-change detector). trigger: Always, for every PR review (cost: one git log of BASE..HEAD). Priority when a memory note or the thread says a draft PR was folded, stacked or fast-forwarded into this one, or when a commit subject starts with Name/Rename/Brace/Clean up/Shorten/Clarify/Reword, or names a test addition. unit of evaluation: the SIDE commit, not the hunk. Procedure: (1) BASE = main side of the last merge, HEAD = reviewed head; save the title and 'What changes'. (2) git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short --no-merges BASE..HEAD; mark MAIN-FEATURE (subject names a type, function, Note or behaviour of the title or 'What changes') or SIDE (rename, naming pass, braces, comment wording, test addition, or hunks of a folded draft outside its own files). (3) Identifier set written by hand from the body and the new headers, each confirmed with grep -c in the diff. (4) Rename map of symbol pairs the PR replaced on existing lines. (5) For each SIDE commit, for each file, for each hunk: count '-' lines that exist verbatim at BASE, EXCLUDING blank, brace-only and comment-only lines. CANDIDATE when at least half of the '-' lines and at least one non-comment '-' line exist at BASE, and the '+' lines carry no identifier. A hunk with no non-comment '-' line at BASE is polish of PR lines or a comment rewrite: not a candidate; if the comment describes a PR behaviour it is in scope, otherwise at most a wording nit. (5b) Attach: a candidate hunk that sits in the same commit and the same function or TEST_CASE as a non-candidate hunk carrying an identifier inherits that hunk's status (in scope). (6) Clearance, token level: a '-'/'+' pair is cleared only when the '-' line with the rename map applied equals the '+' line. A review thread of THIS PR that asked for the change clears it (cite the id). A body sentence clears a hunk only when it describes the hunk's ADDED content (the new constant name, the new check, the new behaviour); a sentence that merely names the file or the callee as an existing caller or test ('t_heap_v2 also tests it directly') does not clear; a sentence that says the opposite ('The tile loads are unchanged') is quoted as a contradiction. (7) Revert test for each remaining hunk: patch -R the commit's hunk onto HEAD:FILE; record whether any body sentence stops being true, whether any identifier stops compiling or being tested, and by how many lines diff(BASE, reverted) shrinks. (8) Test assertions among the remaining hunks: name the callee. Callee absent from git diff BASE..HEAD and no identifier -> unrelated. Callee rewritten by the PR -> regression guard; report only as BODY GAP ('the body never says <callee> keeps <contract>; add the sentence or move the check with the <feature> change'), never as unrelated. (9) One finding, one ask: split-out findings, the squash request and body-gap findings are separate. discriminating_question: both must hold: (a) the hunk changes non-comment lines that exist verbatim at BASE (at least half of its '-' lines), and (b) reverting it alone leaves every body sentence true and every PR identifier compiling and tested. false_positive_guard: do not flag a pair that differs only by the rename map; any hunk whose '-' lines are absent from BASE or are comments only (new headers, new Notes, new tests, Note rewordings, the naming passes on PR-added lines); a comment or constant hunk in the same commit and function as an in-scope hunk that carries an identifier (707159b9ef's poison comment); a change a reviewer of THIS PR asked for; a cleanup the title or 'What changes' lists as bundled; a test whose callee the PR rewrote (body-gap at most). A body sentence that names a file as an existing caller or test is not a claim and does not clear. finding_template: '<file>:<lines at HEAD> (commit <id>, "<subject>") changes <N> non-comment lines that exist at BASE and that <feature> does not touch: <what it does>. Reverting it alone keeps the body true (body:<line> says "<sentence>") and nothing the PR introduces stops compiling. Not part of <PR title>: please split it into its own PR.'

rule.name: Commit history is reviewed content
rule.trigger: Any PR review where git rev-list --count base..head is greater than about 5, or any PR that went through one or more review rounds with fix commits, or whose body contains a commit-per-thread table.
procedure: 1. Count and list: run `git rev-list --count <base>..<head>` and `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso <base>..<head>`. Also run `git log --first-parent --oneline <base>..<head>` and note every merge commit (merge of main, merge of another PR into the branch).

2. Learn how main lands PRs: run `git log --first-parent --oneline -20 origin/main`. If the lines read 'Merge pull request #...', branch commits become permanent main history and the rule applies in full. If main shows one squashed commit per PR, downgrade to a note.

3. Group the commits: for each file, run `git log --format='%h %s' <base>..<head> -- <file>`; for each commit run `git show --stat <id>`. Mark a commit as FIXUP when (a) its subject names a Note, comment, constant, or function that an earlier commit of the same PR introduced and it changes only text or names (subjects starting Reword, Tighten, Clarify, Shorten, Rename, Name the ..., Review fixes), or (b) it removes or reverts something an earlier commit of the same PR added (e.g. daf227de13 removes an assert b951ba9b4c added), or (c) its commit message says 'same facts, comment only' or cites a review thread id as its reason.
4. Count FIXUP commits and clusters: two or more FIXUP commits touching the same Note or comment is a cluster (here a52ce4db25, 55f0068cbf, 34b157326f on Note [DMA allocation creates objects]).
5. Name the topical units of the PR from the diff (here: typed views + kernels + call sites; DMA allocation creates the blocks; tests). Compare the unit count with the commit count.
6. Read the PR body for a commit-by-thread table or 'Commits on top of <id>' section. Its presence confirms the history is review narration; it is also a pr-description-no-history violation.

7. Report the count, the FIXUP ids grouped by what they rewrite, the merge commits, how main lands PRs, and the proposed topical commit list. Keep separate any commit of another author taken by fast-forward (8bbbb7c82d, PR #4697) and say its authorship should survive the squash.
rule.discriminating_question: Would a reader of `git log main` later learn anything from this commit that the neighbouring commits of the same PR do not already give them? A commit that exists only because an earlier commit of the same PR was wrong or badly worded is fixup history, not a topical unit, and should not land on main.
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag when: main squash-merges on landing (then say 'optional, history is discarded at merge'); the commits are distinct topical units that a bisect would want kept apart (separate feature, separate bug fix, a maintainer's PR taken by fast-forward with its authorship); the PR is a draft and the author has already stated a squash is pending; or there is only one FIXUP commit. Do not count a merge of main as a fixup. Do not demand one single commit when the PR has two or more real units.
rule.finding_template: Commits: <N> in <base>..<head>, <K> of them rewriting <the same Note / comment / constant set> (<ids, oldest first>), plus <M> merge commits. main lands PRs by merge commit, so each one becomes permanent history. Please squash into topical commits: <unit 1>, <unit 2>, <unit 3>; keep <other-author commit id> as its own commit. Drop the commit-per-thread table from the body.

votes.fix:
Rule name: Commit history is reviewed content (fixup clusters and unrelated commits).

Trigger: run steps 1-3 on every PR review (four git commands, no judgment). Report a finding only when step 3 yields a CLUSTER (two or more FIXUP commits rewriting the same Note, comment, name set, or function) or an UNRELATED commit. A long history with no cluster and no unrelated commit gets at most a one-line note (precedent: PR 4596 landed with 26 commits, 13 subjects carrying "review round", and Wade approved it without a squash request on 2026-09-30).

Procedure:
1. Base and head. Base = the merge-base of the head and the PR's target branch. If the PR is stacked (target is not main, or the body names a parent PR), base = the parent PR's head, so the lower PR's commits are not counted. Run `git rev-list --count <base>..<head>`, `git rev-list --count --no-merges <base>..<head>`, and `git log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=iso <base>..<head>`. Record both counts; the finding states which one it uses ("N commits, M of them merges").
2. How the target branch lands PRs: `git log --first-parent --oneline -20 origin/main`. Squash-merge signature = one parent and a subject ending "(#NNN)". Merge signature = "Merge pull request #NNN". On merge-landing branches every branch commit becomes permanent history and the finding is a request; on squash-landing branches the finding is a note ("optional, history is discarded at merge").
3. Bin every non-merge commit. Run `git show --stat --format='%h %an%n%b' <id>` for each.
   - OTHER-AUTHOR: author differs from the PR author (here 8bbbb7c82d and 63df10cf90 by Ben Gamari). Never a fixup; the finding says to keep its authorship.
   - FIXUP: (a) the body cites a review thread id, a round, or says "comment only" / "same facts" (grep %b for `[0-9]{10}|review|round|comment.only`); or (b) every file it touches was already touched by an earlier commit of the same PR and the subject starts with Reword, Tighten, Clarify, Shorten, Rename, Name the, Drop, Fix, Review fixes; or (c) it removes or reverts a line that an earlier commit of the same PR added (`git log -S'<removed line>' <base>..<id>` hits an earlier PR commit).
   - UNRELATED: the commit's file set is disjoint from the file set of every other non-fixup commit of the PR and the subject does not name the PR's topic (here ec795fbce8, only src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp). Verdict for this bin is "split out", not "squash".
   - UNIT: everything else.
   A CLUSTER = two or more FIXUP commits whose stat lists the same file and whose subjects or bodies name the same Note, comment, or name set (here a52ce4db25, 55f0068cbf, 34b157326f on Note [DMA allocation creates objects]; fcdbfff8e4, 2280e4beb2, 76502ce5b2 on the packed V comments; 1c87d66926, 5051264d80 on named values).
4. Topical units (the only judgment step, derived, not invented): one unit per PR body section heading that names a code change, merged with the file-set groups of the UNIT commits. Here: typed views + kernels + call sites; DMA allocation creates the blocks; tests. Compare the unit count with the non-merge count.
5. Read the PR body for a commit-per-thread table or a "Commits on top of <id>" section. Its presence confirms the history is review narration. Report it under the PR-description point, not inside this finding.

Discriminating question (replaces the old one): Does this commit exist only because an earlier commit of the SAME PR was wrong or badly worded (FIXUP), or because it belongs to a DIFFERENT PR (UNRELATED)? A commit that a `git bisect` would want kept apart from its neighbours, with its own behaviour change and its own author, is a UNIT and stays.

False-positive guard: do not report when the target branch squash-merges (note only); when the only FIXUP commits are singletons with no cluster; when the PR is a draft or the author has already written that a squash is pending; when the commits are by another author (keep them, with authorship); when the PR is stacked and the extra commits are the parent PR's. Do not count a merge of main or a merge of another PR as a fixup. Do not demand one commit when step 4 found two or more units. Do not raise severity above hygiene: on this repo maintainers have let 19-commit (PR 3879) and 26-commit (PR 4596) histories land.

Finding template (Wade's shape: one count, one observation, one ask): "Commits: <N> (<M> merges), <K> of them rewording <the same Note / the packed V comments> (<ids, oldest first>). Please squash into <unit 1>, <unit 2>, <unit 3>; keep <other-author id> as its own commit." For an UNRELATED commit, a separate line: "<id> (<subject>) touches only <file> and is not part of <PR topic>; please split it out." The commit-per-thread table in the body goes under the PR-description finding.

probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Commit history is reviewed content (fixup clusters and unrelated commits).

Trigger: run the four git commands and the binning below on every PR review, and again at every push after a review round and at the final head before requesting review. Report a finding only when the binning yields (i) a CLUSTER: two or more FIXUP commits whose subject or body names the same Note, comment block or constant set, or (ii) an UNRELATED commit. A long history with neither gets at most a one-line note (precedent: Wade approved PR 4596 at 26 commits). Base = merge-base with the target branch; for a stacked PR, base = the parent PR's head. Record both 'rev-list --count' and '--no-merges', and the count at the head the reviewer saw if that differs from the current head (here 20 at c12df586b6, 21 at 96a6220ab6).

Binning (content first, subject words are only a hint):
- OTHER-AUTHOR: %an differs from the PR author, on either side of a merge (8bbbb7c82d and 63df10cf90 by Ben Gamari). Never counted; the finding says to keep them with authorship.
- FIXUP requires BOTH: (1) the diff changes no behavior: comment, whitespace or name-only changes, or an exact restore of main's behavior (daf227de13 restores main's assert-free path), checked with `git show -w --stat` and by reading the hunks; and (2) the reason is an earlier commit of the SAME PR: the subject or body names a Note, comment or constant that an earlier PR commit introduced, or the body cites a review thread id, 'comment only' or 'same facts'. A subject prefix (Reword, Tighten, Clarify, Shorten, Rename, Name the, Review fixes, Drop) alone never bins a commit.
- UNIT: a commit that adds or removes behavior or code with a rationale in its body, even when it replaces code an earlier PR commit added (39a6899446 replaces construct_kv_blocks with the allocation; c12df586b6 removes v_vnni_row; 959d1ae229 adds the partner-zero assertions; 707159b9ef adds the parity bit checks). The old criterion 'removes something an earlier commit added' is dropped as a FIXUP test. When a UNIT is squashed into a larger unit, its rationale paragraph goes into the squashed message.
- UNRELATED: every line the commit replaces already existed at the base (check with `git show <base>:<file> | grep` for the replaced text) and no UNIT commit of the PR depends on the change (ec795fbce8: the 18 '/* dest tile */' literals exist at e5fa372c19). Verdict is 'split out', never 'squash'. A hunk of a UNIT commit that touches a file outside the PR's topic (t_heap_v2.cpp in 39a6899446) is reported under the 'unrelated changes' point, not here.
- CLUSTER: two or more FIXUP commits whose stat lists the same file and whose subjects or bodies name the same Note, comment block or constant set (here: a52ce4db25, 55f0068cbf, 34b157326f on Note [DMA allocation creates objects]; fcdbfff8e4, 2280e4beb2, 76502ce5b2 on the packed V comments; 1c87d66926, 5051264d80 on the named values). Name every cluster, oldest first.

Guard (no finding): the target branch squash-merges (then a note 'optional, history is discarded at merge'; merge-landing signature on this repo = every recent first-parent commit reads 'Merge pull request #'); no cluster and no unrelated commit; the PR is a draft or the author has written that a squash is pending; the extra commits belong to a parent PR of a stack or to another author. The commit-per-thread table in the PR body is reported under the PR-description point only, never inside this finding.

Finding template (one count, one observation, one ask): 'Commits: <N> (<M> merges) at <head>, <K> of them rewording <Note / comment block> (<ids, oldest first>). Please squash into <unit 1>, <unit 2>, <unit 3>; keep <other-author ids> as their own commits.' For an UNRELATED commit, a separate line: '<id> (<subject>) touches only <file> and replaces code that main already had; please split it out.'

rule.name: CI claims name the lane, the trigger and the configure line
rule.trigger: A PR body, PR comment, README or source comment sentence that says what 'CI' (or 'the required checks', 'the build job', 'the nightly') builds, runs, covers, requires or lacks: a CMake option, a preset, a platform, a compiler, a test binary, 'AMX-on/off'. Also any reviewer comment that cites a workflow file:line as proof about CI, and any PR number offered as the date a CI setting changed.
procedure: 1. Collect the claims. In the PR body (gh pr view N --json body -q .body > body.md), the changed README*.md files and changed comments: grep -n -i -E 'CI|workflow|required|lane|nightly|preset|build job' body.md. Write each claim as: subject lane (if named), flag or setting, asserted value, cited PR or commit (if any).

2. List the workflows and their triggers at the main side of the head: for f in $(git ls-tree --name-only <main> .github/workflows/); do echo $f; git show <main>:$f | sed -n '/^on:/,/^[a-z]/p' | grep -E '^\s*(pull_request|merge_group|push|schedule|workflow_dispatch|workflow_call|cron)'; done. Also list who calls a workflow_call-only file: git grep -n 'uses: ./.github/workflows/' <main> -- .github.

3. Find every place the setting lives: git grep -n '<FLAG>' <main> -- .github nix flake.nix GNUmakefile CMakePresets.json CMakeLists.txt README.ci.md. Map each hit to the lane that consumes the file (a yml configure line -> that workflow; nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix -> gcp-nix.yml; CMakePresets.json deb -> `make deb` in publish-deb.yml). Note the CMakeLists.txt default for the option.

4. Get the gating set from GitHub, not from the repo: gh pr checks <N> --repo positron-ai/tron --required, and gh pr checks <N> --json name,workflow,state. The workflow column names the lane(s) whose configure line decides the claim. (Branch-protection APIs may be 404 for non-admins; the check list is the substitute.)

5. Compare per claim: (a) the gating lane's configure line has the setting or not; (b) any non-gating lane that has the setting, with its trigger (cron, tags, dispatch); (c) the PR number the body cites against git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -S'<FLAG>' -- <file> and git log --merges --ancestry-path <commit>..<main> | tail -1 (the merge that brought it).

6. Decide: a claim that is true for the gating lane but names no lane, while another lane with the opposite setting exists in the repo, is a finding (ambiguous and will be read as false). A claim false for the gating lane is a finding. A wrong PR number or date is a finding.

7. Write the finding with the lane, the trigger, the configure line (file:line) and the merge commit of the setting, and give the replacement sentence verbatim. If a reviewer cited a line in a non-gating workflow, say so in the reply instead of conceding.
rule.discriminating_question: Which workflow file gates this PR (from `gh pr checks --required`), under which trigger, and does that workflow's configure line carry the setting the sentence asserts?
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag a sentence that names the lane and trigger and matches that lane's configure line (for example 'the GCP Nix lane that gates PRs builds without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH'). Do not flag because a reviewer cited a workflow line, when that workflow is not in the PR's check list: answer the reviewer with the trigger block instead. Do not flag a generic 'CI is green' sentence that asserts no configuration. Do not treat README.ci.md as the source of truth; it is a claim to check by the same steps.
rule.finding_template: <location, e.g. PR body, Words row 'AMX-on build, AMX-off build'>: '<quoted sentence>' names no lane. The checks that gate this PR are <lane, from gh pr checks --required>, configured in <file:line> <with | without> <FLAG> (so <value>). <Other lane file:line> passes <FLAG>=<value> but runs only on <trigger> (<caller file:line>) since <cutover commit>; the setting entered it in <commit> via PR #<n> (<date>). Replace with: '<exact sentence naming lane, trigger and setting>'.

votes.fix:
Keep the rule name, trigger and steps 2, 3, 6 as they are. Replace the rest as follows.

Discriminating question (replaces the old one): "List every lane in the repo that sets or omits this setting, with its trigger. Do the lanes agree? If they disagree, does the sentence say which lane it means, and does that lane's configure line (file:line) match the sentence?" A sentence is a finding when the lanes disagree and the sentence names none, or when it names one and that lane's configure line contradicts it, or when it dates the setting to the wrong PR.

Step 1 (replace the grep): grep -n -E '\bCI\b|\bci\b|workflow|required check|lane|nightly|preset|build job|runner' body.md README*.md and the changed comment hunks. Record per hit: lane named (or 'none'), setting, asserted value, cited PR or commit, and whether the claim is about configuration (a flag, preset, compiler) or about runner hardware (a CPU feature, a device).

Step 4 (replace): (a) gh pr checks <N> --repo positron-ai/tron --json name,workflow,state,isRequired. The workflow column names the gating workflow(s). Jobs still waiting (for example behind 'Wait for lab cache' in gcp-nix.yml) do not appear; the build job's name comes from the workflow file, not from the list. (b) From each gating workflow file, follow the build step to its configure line with commands, not memory: git show <main>:.github/workflows/<wf>.yml | grep -n -E 'cmake|preset|nix build|nix run|\.#|uses: \./' ; for a nix attribute, git grep -n '<attribute or .nix file>' <main> -- flake.nix nix/ ; stop at the file:line that holds the -D flags or the preset name. Record file:line and whether the setting is present (else the CMakeLists.txt default).

Step 5(c) (replace): for the PR that brought the setting into a file, run gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number' on the commit from git log -S; this works for merge-queue and squash merges alike. The ancestry-merge command stays as a fallback when gh is unavailable.

New step 5(d), runner hardware claims: a sentence about what the runners have or lack (AMX, FPGA, a GPU) is not decidable from the repo. Record the gating build job's runs-on labels (file:line) and look for a job log line or a runner inventory the author cites. If none exists, the verdict is 'unverified from the repo; cite a job log or runner inventory or drop the sentence', never 'true' or 'false'.

False-positive guard, add two items: (1) when every lane in the repo agrees on the setting, a sentence that names no lane is not a finding; (2) a runner-hardware sentence is reported as unverified, not as false, unless a job log or inventory contradicts it.

probe.tightened_rule:
Name: CI claims name the lane, the trigger and the configure line.

Trigger (all three parts must hold for one sentence): (1) the sentence has a CI subject: the word CI, 'required checks', 'the build job', 'the nightly', 'runner(s)', a workflow name (gcp-nix, cmake-single-platform, publish-deb, 'GCP Nix', 'deb lane'), or a PR label that a workflow reads ('Skip benchmarks', 'Run CI'); (2) it asserts a setting or coverage: a CMake option, a preset, a compiler, a test binary, a platform feature, 'AMX-on/off', 'benchmarks run/skipped'; (3) it is in the PR body, a PR comment, a README*.md hunk or a source-comment hunk of the diff. Also fires on a reviewer comment that cites a .github/workflows file:line as proof about what gates the PR, and on a PR number offered as the date a setting changed when that setting has a hit in .github, nix/, flake.nix, CMakePresets.json or README.ci.md (run `git grep -n '<SETTING>' <main> -- .github nix flake.nix CMakePresets.json README.ci.md` first; no hit means the sentence dates a source change, out of scope).

Step 1 keyword list (replaces 'CI|lane|required'): `grep -n -E '\bCI\b|required check|build job|nightly|workflow|preset|runner|gcp-nix|GCP Nix|cmake-single|publish-deb|deb lane|Skip benchmarks|Run CI|TRON_[A-Z_]+=(ON|OFF)'` over body.md, changed README*.md and the added comment lines of the diff. Do not grep 'lane' or case-insensitive 'ci': in tron 'lane' is a 32-bit SIMD slot and 'plane' contains 'lane'.

Discriminating question: list every lane in the repo that sets or omits this setting, with its trigger block. Do the lanes agree? If they disagree, does the sentence say which lane it means, and does that lane's configure line (file:line) match the sentence? A finding exists when the lanes disagree and the sentence names none, when it names a lane whose configure line contradicts it, or when it dates the setting to a PR that did not touch the file where the setting lives (check with `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number'` on the commit from `git log -S`).

Guards (no finding): (a) the sentence names the lane and trigger and matches that lane's configure line; (b) every lane in the repo agrees on the setting; (c) a reviewer cites a workflow line whose workflow is not in `gh pr checks --json workflow` for a finished run: reply with the on: block and caller file:line, do not concede; (d) a generic 'CI is green' sentence; (e) a sentence about builds the author made (a named tree such as gen/gen-amxoff, a named machine such as delphi-3bda, a runtron arm, a kill-switch run) is a measurement statement, not a CI claim; (f) a runtime log or WARN string in code ('AMX unavailable on this host') is not a claim; (g) SIMD 'lane', 'plane', '16-lane build' and 'AVX-512 ... lane' sentences are layout prose; (h) a PR-label sentence that matches AGENTS.md or README.ci.md and the workflow's label check (for example gcp-nix.yml:726) is a documented policy, record it as verified; (i) README.ci.md is a claim to check, never the source of truth. Step 4 reads `gh pr checks <N> --json name,workflow,state,isRequired` on a finished run only: while 'Wait for lab cache' or 'Build Tron' is IN_PROGRESS the downstream GCP Nix jobs are absent and the build job's name must come from the workflow file.

Finding template (two to three sentences, provenance stays in the review's evidence block): '<location>: "<quoted sentence>" names no lane. The checks on this PR come from <gating workflow>, configured at <file:line> <with | without> <FLAG> (<default and its file:line>); <other file:line> passes <FLAG>=<value> but runs only from <caller or trigger>. Please say which, for example: "<replacement sentence naming lane and setting>".' Example on L4a: 'PR body, Words row "AMX-on build, AMX-off build": "the configuration the required CI builds" names no lane. The checks on this PR come from gcp-nix.yml, configured at nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80-100 without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (default OFF, CMakeLists.txt:46); cmake-single-platform.yml:355 passes ON but runs only from publish-deb.yml:68 and manual dispatch. Please say which, for example: "OFF is what the GCP Nix lane that gates PRs builds; the nightly deb lane and the deb preset build ON."'

rule.name: Result rows cite the reviewed head
rule.trigger: The PR description (or any report pasted into it) contains test, token-identity, performance, objdump or lint results with a commit id, OR the head moved after any such row was written (push, merge of main, rebase, amend, squash). Also fires when the body uses 'the head', 'now', 'current' next to a commit id.
procedure: 1. Fetch the body and the head: `gh pr view N --json body,headRefOid -q .body > body.md`; `HEAD=$(gh pr view N --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)`; note the head commit date: `git -C WT log -1 --format=%cI $HEAD`.
2. List every commit id the body names: `grep -oE '\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b' body.md | sort -u`. Drop ids that appear only in a commit-history or review-thread table (those name commits, not results).

3. For each remaining id: `git -C WT cat-file -t ID` (exists?), `git -C WT rev-list --count ID..$HEAD` (commits behind the head), and the PR files that changed between them: `comm -12 <(git -C WT diff --name-only ID $HEAD | sort) <(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE $HEAD | sort)` where BASE is the main side of the merge or the merge-base.

4. Build a table, one row per result sentence or table row: result kind (unit test, token identity, perf A/B, objdump, lint), cited id, cited baseline (main id), date, label ('pre-merge', 'pre-rebase', none).

5. Compare each row: cited id == $HEAD? baseline main id == the main side merged into the head? If either is no and the label is none, it is a finding. If the label is present, check that the body also states why the row still applies (which PR files did not change between ID and $HEAD, from step 3).
6. Check the prose around each id for 'the head', 'now', 'current', 'latest': flag when the id is not $HEAD.
7. Check dates: if the head commit date is later than every result date in the body, every row is pre-head; report it once for the whole section.
8. Report per result kind, with the count of commits behind and the overlapping files from step 3 as the reason a re-run matters.
rule.discriminating_question: For each result row in the body, is the cited commit id the reviewed head (or, if not, is the row labelled with its older id AND does the body say why the result still applies or when the re-run happens)?
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag an id that equals the head. Do not flag a row explicitly labelled pre-merge or pre-rebase that also states why it still applies (for example: the commits between touch no file the test binary compiles, verified with git diff --name-only, not assumed). Do not flag ids in the 'Commits' or 'Review comments and their outcome' tables; they name commits, not measurements. Do not flag the baseline main id when it is the merge-base of the head. A rebuilt-and-rerun row with the same numbers is not stale even if the numbers did not change.
rule.finding_template: PR description, <section>: the <unit-test | token-identity | perf A/B | objdump> rows cite <id>, <N> commits before the head <head> (the merge of main <main id> changed <files from step 3>); the text calls <id> 'the head'. Re-run at <head>, or label the rows pre-merge and say which files did not change between the two.

votes.fix:
Name: Result rows cite the reviewed head.

Trigger: the PR body (or a report pasted into it) has a Verification, Status, Test or Results section that names a commit id, or a result row (test counts, token identity, perf A/B, objdump, lint) with no id at all.

Procedure:
1. `gh pr view N --json body -q .body > body.md`; `HEAD=$(gh pr view N --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)`; `git -C WT fetch -q origin main`; `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD origin/main)` (works for a merge head, a rebase and a squash alike); `PRFILES=$(git -C WT diff --name-only $BASE $HEAD | sort)`.
2. Candidate ids: `grep -oE '\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b' body.md | sort -u`. Keep an id only if `git -C WT cat-file -t ID` prints `commit` (this drops GitHub review/comment numbers such as 4134076112). Drop ids whose every occurrence is inside a Commits table or a review-thread table (they name commits, not measurements).
3. For each kept id: ANCESTOR = `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor ID $HEAD`; if yes, BEHIND = `git -C WT rev-list --count ID..$HEAD`, else BEHIND = 'not an ancestor (amended, rebased or squashed)'. CHANGED = `comm -12 <(git -C WT diff --name-only ID $HEAD | sort) <(echo "$PRFILES")` = PR files whose content differs between the cited id and the head. If CHANGED is empty, the result still applies by construction; note it, the only ask is a label.
4. Table, one row per result sentence or table row: kind (unit test, token identity, perf A/B, objdump, lint, build), cited id (or 'none'), cited comparison baseline (main id, if any), date, label (pre-merge / pre-rebase / none), whether a row of the same kind at $HEAD also exists in the body.
5. Finding conditions: (a) cited id != $HEAD, label none -> finding; (b) cited id != $HEAD, label present, but the body says neither why the row still applies (CHANGED empty, or the test binary compiles none of CHANGED) nor when the re-run happens -> finding; (c) cited id == 'none' -> finding (no provenance); (d) cited id == $HEAD and the comparison baseline is not $BASE -> finding (head measured against an old main). Do not check the baseline of a row already flagged under (a) or (b); it is the same defect.
6. Wording: for each kept id outside the Commits table, read the sentence that contains it. Flag it when the sentence asserts in the present tense that the id is the head or the current state ('ran at the head X', 'now X', 'current X') and X != $HEAD. Past-tense references ('the head the review was made on') are not flagged.
7. Only for rows with no id: compare the row's date with `git -C WT log -1 --format=%cI $HEAD`; a row dated before the head commit cannot be from the head. Skip this when the row has only a date without a time and the head commit is the same day.
8. Report once per result kind: cited id, BEHIND, CHANGED (list), and whether a head row exists.

Discriminating question: for each result row in the body, is the cited commit id the reviewed head? If not: is the row labelled with its older id, and does the body say either why the result still applies (which PR files did not change between the id and the head) or when the re-run happens? A row with no id at all fails too.

False-positive guard: an id equal to $HEAD; a labelled older row whose body text gives the reason or the re-run date; ids in the Commits or review-thread tables; a comparison baseline equal to $BASE, or equal to the merge-base of the row's own cited id when that row is already flagged for its id; a past-tense 'the head' sentence; a row whose CHANGED set is empty is a label-only nit, not a re-run request; rows re-run at the head with unchanged numbers are not stale.

Finding template (two sentences, Wade's form): 'PR description, <section>: the <unit-test / token-identity / perf A/B / objdump> rows cite <id>, <BEHIND> behind the head <head>; the merge of main changed <CHANGED files> since then[, and line <n> calls <id> "the head"]. Please <re-run them at <head> | delete them, the rows at <head> below already replace them | mark them pre-merge and say why they still apply>.'

why_missed.root_cause: Every prior check of the description asked whether a sentence is READABLE (plain-English rules) or TRUE (docs-exports: stale or overstated). None asked whether the sentence is NEEDED by the reviewer of the head. Worse, the author-side rules actively produced the three passages: plain-English rule 3 ('every number gets ... a clause saying what it means') turned the assertion-count delta into a four-sentence reconciliation; the global CLAUDE.md 'Interpret test results with proof' rule ('cite the reference: name the test/run/metric') put the log path and the UTC build windows into the body as citations. Rule 3 rewards adding meaning to a number; it has no companion rule that asks whether the number should be in the document at all. The pr-description-no-history rule (present tense, provenance = commit id + date) existed since 2026-09-30 but was recorded as feedback on PR 4596 and never turned into a check that runs on a PR body; the 2026-09-22 lenses (find:prose) scoped 'comments, Notes and plain English' to source files, and find:callers only suggested ADDING a sentence to the body.
why_missed.author_blind_spot: The same agent that ran the 3bda campaign wrote the Status section from its own run log, so every number it had (timestamps, log path, assertion deltas) looked like evidence worth keeping; its success criterion was 'every claim grounded', not 'every sentence earns its place for a reader who cannot open delphi-3bda'. The description was also written incrementally across rounds (c73e7fb2f9 -> faf8ee42ca -> c12df586b6 -> 96a6220ab6), so each round appended its proof paragraph and nobody re-read the section as a stranger. A reviewer reads the body once, top to bottom, with no access to the machine; from that seat the arithmetic is noise and the log path is unverifiable.

rule.name: pr-body-reader-value
rule.trigger: Any PR description (or PR comment meant as the record) that contains a Status, Verification, Tests or Results section, or any sentence with a wall-clock time, a hostname-local path, a commit id that is not a PR commit, or an arithmetic reconciliation of two counts.
procedure: 1. Fetch the live body: gh pr view <N> --repo positron-ai/tron --json body -q .body > body.md (or use the saved copy the task names). Number the lines: cat -n body.md.
2. Fetch the PR commit list: gh pr view <N> --json commits -q '.commits[].oid' > pr-commits.txt. Also note the head sha.

3. Scan body.md for the four markers with one grep: grep -n -E '[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})? ?(UTC|Z)|/var/tmp|/tmp/|/home/|[0-9]+ [+-] [0-9]+ = [0-9]+|= [0-9]+ matches|fewer assertions|more assertions|rc [0-9]' body.md. Record every hit with its line number.

4. For every 7-to-12 hex commit id in the body (grep -o -E '\b[0-9a-f]{7,12}\b' body.md | sort -u), check it against pr-commits.txt and against main: git -C <worktree> branch -a --contains <id>. An id that no branch contains is a dangling amend; an id that is not in the PR list and not on main is unreachable for the reader.

5. For each hit from steps 3-4, write the reader test in one line: 'If this clause were deleted, which decision of a reviewer who can only open GitHub would change?' Allowed answers: (a) it identifies the binary or commit the result belongs to (keep, as commit id + date); (b) it is the pass/fail result itself (keep); (c) nothing changes (flag).

6. votes.fix:
Rule pr-body-reader-value (corrected).

Trigger: a PR description or record comment with a Status / Verification / Tests / Results section.

Procedure:
1. Save the live body: gh pr view <N> --repo positron-ai/tron --json body -q .body > body.md; cat -n body.md.
2. Save the PR commit list and head: gh pr view <N> --json commits,headRefOid -q '.commits[].oid, .headRefOid' > pr-commits.txt. Fetch main: git -C <worktree> fetch origin main.
3. Scan for clutter markers (no 'rc' marker; rc lines are the keep anchor): grep -n -E '[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})? ?(UTC|Z)|/var/tmp/|/tmp/|/home/|[0-9]+ [+-] [0-9]+ = [0-9]+|= [0-9]+ matches|(fewer|more) assertions than' body.md. Record line numbers.
4. Commit ids: grep -o -E '\b[0-9a-f]{7,12}\b' body.md | grep -E '[a-f]' | sort -u (drop all-digit tokens: GitHub comment, review and issue ids). For each id: (i) git cat-file -e <id>^{commit} || mark 'not a commit, skip'; (ii) reachable = id prefix-matches a line of pr-commits.txt OR git merge-base --is-ancestor <id> origin/main. An id that exists but is not reachable is unreachable for a GitHub reader (a dangling amend or a local backup branch). Hand off: an unreachable id that labels a test or token-identity RESULT belongs to the pre-merge-results item (L4b: re-run or mark pre-merge); an id inside a commit-history or review-outcome table belongs to the squash / no-history item. Only the remaining hits stay in this rule.
5. For each remaining hit, answer in one line: 'Deleting this clause changes which decision of a reviewer who can only open GitHub?' Allowed answers: (a) it names the commit a result belongs to -> keep as commit id + date; (b) it is the pass/fail outcome or the count of a run at the head -> keep; (c) nothing -> flag. Flagging a clause means deleting the whole sentence or rewriting it, never leaving a fragment.
6. Bin every flagged clause: bin 1 wall-clock time (keep the date only); bin 2 machine-local path or log name (delete; the rc/outcome sentence stays); bin 3 count reconciliation between two revisions (delete the arithmetic; keep at most one sentence 'no production assertion was removed' if the reviewer needs it).
7. History check: a clause comparing the head with an earlier revision of the same PR ('fewer than at <sha>', 'before its last amend', 'the same commit before') is bin 3 even when the numbers are right.
8. Report once per section, ask first.

Discriminating question (unchanged): if the reviewer cannot open the machine, the log or the earlier revision, does deleting this clause change any decision about the head? No -> it goes.

False-positive guard (unchanged plus): never flag all-digit ids, '#NNNN' issue/PR numbers, URLs, repo-relative paths (t/t_llama_unit.cpp), public artifact links, a commit id + date on a measurement, pass/fail outcomes and counts at the head, or a time range when the duration is the measured quantity. Do not judge arithmetic correctness. Do not apply to source comments or to status/ campaign pages.

Finding template (Wade shape, ask first): 'PR description, Status section lines <a>-<b>: the build timestamps, the log path on <host> and the <X = Y + Z> assertion reconciliation against <sha> can go. Keep `<test> rc 0 at <head sha>` and the test rows at the head. A reviewer on GitHub cannot open the host, the log or <sha>, and none of these clauses changes a decision about the head.'

probe.tightened_rule:
Rule pr-body-reader-value (tightened).

Trigger: a PR description, or a PR comment meant as the record, that has a Status, Verification, Tests or Results section. The procedure runs ONLY inside those sections (cut body.md to the section line ranges first); the What-changes, Words-used-here and reviewer-response sections are out of scope for this rule (history narration there belongs to the pr-description-no-history rule and to the squash item).

Procedure:
1. Save the body under review (the saved copy the task names, or gh pr view <N> --json body) and number it: cat -n body.md. Mark the line ranges of the Status/Verification/Tests/Results sections.
2. Build the commit list of the REVIEWED head, not the live PR: git -C <worktree> rev-list <base>..<reviewed head> > pr-commits.txt (the live gh commit list is wrong after a squash or force-push). git fetch origin.
3. Within the section ranges, grep -n -E '[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})? ?(UTC|Z)|/var/tmp/|/tmp/|/home/|[0-9]+ [+-] [0-9]+ = [0-9]+|= [0-9]+ matches|(fewer|more) assertions than|before its last amend'. No 'rc' marker: rc clauses are the keep anchor.
4. Commit ids within the section ranges: grep -o -E '\b[0-9a-f]{7,12}\b' | grep -E '[a-f]' | sort -u (all-digit tokens are GitHub comment, review and issue ids: never flag). For each id: (i) git cat-file -e <id>^{commit} or skip; (ii) reachable = prefix of a line in pr-commits.txt, OR git merge-base --is-ancestor <id> origin/main, OR git branch -r --contains <id> prints an origin/ ref (GitHub shows any pushed commit); an id with no origin ref is dangling. Hand off before step 5: a dangling or non-PR id that labels a test or token-identity RESULT goes to the pre-merge-results item (re-run at the head or mark pre-merge); an id inside a commit-history or review-outcome table goes to the squash / no-history item; a reachable id that only says which binary produced a measurement is provenance and stops here. Only ids left after the hand-off continue.
5. For every remaining step-3 and step-4 hit, answer in one line: 'If a reviewer who can open only GitHub lost this clause, which decision about the head would change?' (a) it names the commit a result belongs to: keep as commit id + date; (b) it is the pass/fail outcome or a count of a run at the head: keep; (c) nothing: flag the whole sentence (never leave a fragment).
6. Bin the flagged clauses: bin 1 clock times (keep the calendar date only); bin 2 machine-local paths and log names (delete; the rc/outcome sentence stays); bin 3 count reconciliation or comparison against an earlier revision of the same PR (delete the arithmetic; keep at most one sentence 'no production assertion was removed' if the reviewer needs it).
7. History check inside the sections: 'fewer than at <sha>', 'before its last amend', 'the same commit before', 'first revision ..., now ...' are bin 3 even when the numbers are right. The positron-code-review narration test applies to the PR body too.
8. Report once per section, ask first: 'PR description, <section> lines <a>-<b>: the build timestamps, the log path on <host> and the <X = Y + Z> reconciliation against <sha> can go. Keep `<test> rc 0 at <head sha>` and the test rows at the head.'

Discriminating question: if the reviewer cannot open the machine, the log or the earlier revision, does deleting this clause change any decision about the head? No means it goes.

False-positive guard: never flag all-digit ids, '#NNNN' issue or PR numbers, URLs or public artifact links, repo-relative paths (t/t_llama_unit.cpp), a bare hostname ('on delphi-3bda') without a path, PCI addresses ('cards 90:00.0'), a calendar date, a commit id + date on a measurement, pass/fail outcomes and counts at the head, or any clause outside the Status/Verification/Tests/Results sections. A clock-time range ('19:51 to 19:56 UTC') is never a measurement; keep a duration only when the sentence states it as a number with units ('TTFT 53.1 s', 'build 4 min 29 s') and that number is the claim. Do not judge arithmetic correctness. Do not apply to source comments, to code, or to campaign record pages under status/.

rule.name: Role-bearing constant names (suffix convention kept)
rule.trigger: The diff adds or renames a `constexpr` (or `static constexpr`) whose identifier ends in a value suffix: `_<digits>`, `_0X<hex>`, `_TRUE`, `_FALSE`. Also fires when a PR replaces inline `/* comment */` literals with such constants.
procedure: 1. List the candidates: `git diff <base> <head> | grep -nE '^\+.*constexpr .*[A-Z]_(0X[0-9A-F]+|[0-9]+|TRUE|FALSE) *='`. Record file and line at <head> for each (`git show <head>:<file> | grep -n NAME`).

2. For each name, strip the value suffix. The remainder is the stem. Group the candidates by stem within one file. A group of two or more names that share a stem and differ only by the suffix (ACCUMULATOR_TILE_0..3) is a family: continue at step 4 for it.

3. For each single name, test the stem against the guide's clause 'the name explains meaning that is not apparent at the use site': the stem must say what the value IS or what it selects (BF16_BITS, V_ODD_TOKEN_LANE_MASK, PATTERN_BASE, APPENDED_TOKENS). A stem that is a number word, a type name alone, or the word 'value'/'constant' restates the literal and is flagged.

4. For each family, open every use site (`git show <head>:<file> | grep -n 'STEM_'`) and write one line per member saying what that member holds or addresses there (example: QK kernel tile 0 stores to `s_transposed + 0 * TILE_FP32S`, so it holds the K-block-0 scores; PV kernel tile 1 stores to `o + half * 64 + 16`, so it holds output dims 16..31). If the members have distinct roles at the use sites, the family is flagged: propose a role per member in the same form the file already uses for its sibling constants (K_EVEN_BLOCK_TILE_4, P_TILE_4), per kernel when the role differs per kernel.

5. Apply the guide's plain-literal exceptions before flagging a single name: (a) value 0 used as an init, reset, comparison, or empty/disabled value: check with `git grep -n '<lowercase stem> = 0' <head> -- <dir>` whether sibling code spells it as a plain constexpr (t_llama_unit.cpp:3282 `x_bytes = 0` vs :3485 `X_BYTES_0`); (b) a name used only inside `alignas(...)`: `git show <head>:<file> | grep -c NAME`; one use means the guide prefers `alignas(64)`, three or more uses that must change together keep the name.

6. Duplicate check: `git grep -nE '= <value>;' <head> -- h/ src/` and read the hits for an existing constant with the same role (tron::chunk_alignment at h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:52 for a 64-byte alignment). A new suffixed constant that re-spells an existing named value is flagged as a duplicate, with the existing name given.
7. Report each flagged item with: file:line at <head>, the stem, what the use site shows, and the replacement name or the plain literal the guide allows. Never report the suffix itself.
rule.discriminating_question: If the value suffix is deleted, does the remaining stem alone still tell a reader at the use site which constant this is and why that value (a role), or is the suffix the only thing that distinguishes it from its siblings or from the bare literal?
rule.false_positive_guard: Do not flag the value suffix or the uppercase style: the guide line 'Append the variable's value to its name' is jhan's decided convention (PR #3879 precedent, comment 6008399647). Do not flag a single constant whose stem names a role, even a short one (BF16_BITS_16, Q_TILE_6, APPENDED_TOKENS_7, PATTERN_BASE_0X3C00). Do not flag required namings of 1, true and false (N_SLOTS_1, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE): the guide keeps those in named declarations. Do not flag a family whose members are interchangeable at every use site (same role, index is the only meaning) when the comment above the family says so. Do not propose dropping a constant that exists to make a shared requirement change together (three or more alignas/alignof uses).
rule.finding_template: <file>:<line> at <head>: `<NAME_A>..<NAME_D>` share the stem `<STEM>` and differ only by the value; at the use sites member i <holds / addresses: quote the line>. Name the role per member the way `<sibling example in the same file>` does (for example `<ROLE_A>_TILE_0`), or state in the comment why the members are interchangeable. [Single-name form:] `<NAME>` at <file>:<line> restates a value the guide spells plain here (<0 as an empty value / alignas>), and the sibling code at <file>:<line> spells it `<plain form>`; use the plain form, or reuse the existing `<existing constant>` (<its file:line>).

votes.fix:
Rule name: Role-bearing constant names (suffix convention kept).

Trigger: the diff adds or renames a named constant whose identifier ends in a value suffix (_<digits>, _0X<hex>, _TRUE, _FALSE), or replaces an inline `/* comment */` literal with one.

Procedure:
1. List candidates: `git diff <base> <head> | grep -nE '^\\+.*\\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_(0X[0-9A-F]+|[0-9]+|TRUE|FALSE) *='` (no `constexpr` in the pattern: the guide's own bool example has none). Record file:line at <head> for each.
2. Strip the suffix to get the stem. Group by stem within one file. Two or more names with one stem = a family (ACCUMULATOR_TILE_0..3). Names whose stems differ by a word (SPECIALS_EVEN_TOKEN_2 / SPECIALS_ODD_TOKEN_3) are not a family.
3. Family test (executable): for every member, open every use site and write what DATA the member holds or addresses there, quoting the line (QK: `_tile_stored(ACCUMULATOR_TILE_1, s_transposed + 1 * TILE_FP32S, ...)` = K block 1 scores; PV: `_tile_stored(ACCUMULATOR_TILE_1, o + half * 64 + 16, ...)` = output dims 16..31). If the data differs per member, flag the family. Permutability is NOT the test: a family is exempt only when every member holds the same data at every use site (a scratch rotation), and the family comment says so. The ask: per-kernel role names in the sibling form already in the file (K_EVEN_BLOCK_TILE_4 / P_TILE_4 are already per-kernel aliases of tile 4), for example QK `K_BLOCK_0_SCORES_TILE_0` and PV `O_DIMS_0_15_TILE_0`.
4. Single-name test (executable): the stem must contain a role word (what the value is or selects). Flag only a stem that is a number word, a bare type name, or 'VALUE'/'CONST'/'LITERAL'. Every other single stem passes (BF16_BITS, V_ODD_TOKEN_LANE_MASK, PATTERN_BASE, APPENDED_TOKENS, X_BYTES, N_SLOTS).
5. Plain-literal exceptions, applied to single names only:
   (a) value 0: flag only when the use site is an initialization, reset, `== 0` / `!= 0` comparison, or an argument whose parameter name is visible at the use site. A 0 passed as a template or positional argument (`uniform_kv_cache<N_SLOTS_1, geometry, X_BYTES_0>`) keeps its name. Sibling code counts as evidence only when it spells a plain literal `0`; an unsuffixed sibling name (`x_bytes = 0` at t_llama_unit.cpp:3282) is a pre-guide form and is not a precedent.
   (b) alignas: `git grep -n NAME <head>` and count uses outside the definition. One use -> ask for `alignas(<value>)` (guide: a name that merely restates the alignment). Two or more uses -> keep the name; do not judge 'must change together'.
   (c) 1, true, false: keep the name when the value encodes a choice or flag (N_SLOTS_1, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE). Flag only when the literal is the trivial value of its own expression (a shift's 1, a mask-minus-one 1, a branch that always returns true), per jhan's 2026-10-02 PR 4737 decisions; state that this is an extension of those two decisions and let jhan confirm.
