probe.tightened_rule:
Name: Role-bearing constant names (suffix convention kept).

Trigger: the diff adds or renames a named constant whose identifier ends in a value suffix (`_<digits>`, `_0X<hex>`, `_TRUE`, `_FALSE`), or replaces an inline `<literal> /* comment */` argument with such a constant. Also re-run on every suffixed constant of the PR, not only on + lines, when the C++ guide (SKILL.md) changed after the naming commits.

Procedure:
1. List candidates: `git diff <base> <head> | grep -nE '^\+.*\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_(0X[0-9A-F]+|[0-9]+|TRUE|FALSE) *='`. Record file:line at <head>.
2. Strip the suffix; the remainder is the stem. Group by stem within one file. Two or more names with one stem form a family (ACCUMULATOR_TILE_0..3). Stems that differ by any word (SPECIALS_EVEN_TOKEN / SPECIALS_ODD_TOKEN) are not a family.
3. Family test (the only step that produced Wade's finding): for every member open every use site and write what DATA it holds there, quoting the line. If the data differs per member (QK: `s_transposed + i * TILE_FP32S` = K block i scores; PV: `o + half * 64 + 16*i` = output dims 16i..16i+15), flag the family. Exempt only when every member holds the same data at every use site (a scratch rotation) AND the comment above the family says so; 'the tiles hold the running sums' is not such a statement. Ask: per-kernel role names in the sibling form the file already uses (K_EVEN_BLOCK_TILE_4 / P_TILE_4 are per-kernel aliases of tile 4), or keep the shared stem and put the per-kernel meaning at the use site; the choice is jhan's.
4. Single-name test: the stem must contain a role word. Flag only a stem that is a number word, a bare type name, or VALUE/CONST/LITERAL. Every stem in PR 4557 passes.
5. Plain-literal exceptions, single names only: (a) zero: flag only when the use site is an initialization, reset, `== 0`/`!= 0` comparison, or an argument whose parameter name is visible there; a zero passed as a template or positional argument keeps its name; sibling evidence counts only when the sibling spells a literal `0`, never an unsuffixed lowercase name. (b) alignas: count uses outside the definition; one use -> ask for `alignas(<value>)`; two or more -> keep. (c) 1/true/false: keep when the value encodes a choice or flag; flag only a literal that is the trivial value of its own expression.
6. Duplicate check, production code only and in scope only: skip this step for a constant defined inside a TEST_CASE or a test file (a test's size parameters are local by design). For a production constant, `git grep -niE '<role word>' <head> -- h/ src/`, read each named-constant hit, and flag a duplicate only when ALL four hold: same meaning stated by the existing constant's name or comment (an alignment of the same object, not any 64-byte alignment); same value in every build configuration (a computed `max(64, chunk_alignment)` counts as 64 only after checking TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is fixed); the existing constant is reachable at the use site through the file's current includes (v_vnni.hpp cannot reach kv_cache.hpp); and the existing constant is not a mock, plugin, or another function's local. Never grep by value (`= 64;`): it returns cache_line_size, TILE_ROW_BYTES_64 and PAGE_TOKENS_64 for one alignment, and misses computed definitions.
7. One finding per flagged item, one ask each, with file:line at <head> and the quoted use lines. Never report the suffix or the uppercase style.

Discriminating question: (i) Family: delete the suffix from every member; do two or more members now share a name while holding different data at their use sites? If yes, the suffix is doing the stem's work. (ii) Single: is the use site one where the guide spells the value plain (init/reset/comparison 0, one-use alignas, trivial 1/true), or does an in-scope production constant with the same stated meaning and the same value in every build already exist? If neither, the name stands.

False-positive guard: do not flag the suffix or the uppercase style (jhan's decided convention, PR #3879 precedent, comment 6008399647). Do not flag a single stem that carries a role word (BF16_BITS_16, V_ODD_TOKEN_LANE_MASK_0XFFFF0000, APPENDED_TOKENS_7, PATTERN_BASE_0X3C00, X_BYTES_0, HEAD_SIZE_64). Do not flag 1/true/false that encode a choice (N_SLOTS_1, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE). Do not flag a named alignment with two or more uses (V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64). Do not run the duplicate check on test-local constants (HEAD_SIZE_64, ARENA_ALIGNMENT_64, REQUEST_BYTES_1024). Do not call two constants duplicates on value alone, when their values differ in any build, when the existing one is out of scope without a new include, or when it lives in a mock/plugin or another function. Do not use unsuffixed main-branch siblings (`x_bytes = 0`) as precedent for a plain literal. Do not report a family finding as a convention finding: the ask is a role per member, in the file's own sibling form.

themes.theme: Cost on the hot path: avoidable per-call work (allocation, memset, repeated assert, conversion) in decode/prefill loops

quotes.quote: xfer_gofs does some avoidable per-call work on the prefill critical path (a 4096-token 36-layer prefill runs this ~4608 times): ... the ctor memsets the whole batch allocation (up to 128 KiB), but in the common 8-head/128-head-size config the populate loops below overwrite every byte.
`TRON_ASSERT` is compiled into release, so every decode-path GOF completion pays 8 std::function invocations instead of 4. Keep one copy.
This change is forcing a call to `ns_to_cycles` every time through here now, even if the caller asked for an indefinite wait.

negative_space: Corpus composition: 480 inline comments across 117 tron PRs; by content tagging 196 are review-type remarks and 284 are his own-PR annotations, replies ('fixed', 'done', 'I pulled these in') or bot adjudications. Counts above are from the review-type set; the PR 4557 summary-body items (constant names, unrelated changes, squash, description) are not inline comments and are quoted from CONTEXT.md.

Kernel and data-layout internals: in PR 4557 (14 files, 1271 insertions) he left 0 comments on kv_cache.hpp (560 changed lines), v_vnni.hpp (400 new lines), amx_attn.cpp (126) and amx_attn_iface.hpp; all 7 inline comments sit in test files (5), the K-view alias header and memory.hpp. Corpus-wide no comment walks a numeric formula or kernel loop line by line; the math-heavy threads (PR 3385, 2796) are his own refutations of bot findings.

Formatting, whitespace, braces, typos: 0 hits for 'whitespace', 'brace', 'typo'; 'format' appears only in his own 'make format' explanations (PR 1949, 1950, 2495) and one long Markdown line (PR 3386). He never asks for clang-format or brace style.

Benchmark numbers and measurement method: no inline comment asks for a TPS, A/A or perf run; 'benchmark' occurs once as a CI label-name nit (PR 3302). On 4557 he asks only that results be re-run at the merged head or labelled pre-merge (staleness), not how they were measured.

C++ guide rule citations: he never cites the C++ coding guide; the constant-name objection is phrased as readability ('reads no better than the 0 /* dest tile */ it replaces'), and jhan treats it as a taste disagreement. Ben-style points (enum vs bool, >4 params, missing domain abstraction) do not appear in the corpus.

PR description prose: he checks the body for claims that disagree with the code or are stale (CI flag, commit ids) and names what 'can go' (assertion arithmetic, UTC timestamps, log paths); he never comments on wording, structure or plain-English style.

Large redesigns of other people's code: design concerns are posed as questions with two alternatives ('Was per-forward granularity chosen on purpose?', 'Was keying by attention worker index ... deliberate?') and accepted as 'Fine as a first step' with a follow-up PR named; he does not demand an architecture change in-PR.
Security, sanitizers, UB classes: 0 'security' hits; the single UB finding (misaligned V-gather scratch, PR 4128) came with a compiled UBSan reproducer and is the exception.
Commit message wording and history narrative: he asks to squash (4557) and to split unrelated commits, but never reviews a commit message's text.

Logging content and levels in others' code: one request to print head_size (PR 1807) and one error-message argument fix (PR 2903); no requests for more logging or tracing in reviews (his TRACE_EVENT remark on PR 2713 ends 'No action needed, just inquiring').
decision_rules: 'please drop' / 'could be dropped' / 'can this go away?' fires when: (a) a test or check duplicates coverage that already exists (duplicate parity GENERATE, trivial-type checks repeating kv_cache.hpp static_asserts, duplicate pool_worker case); (b) a test pins an implementation detail or today's rounding with no named consumer, or pins behaviour the repo policy calls corruption (NaN->+inf row vs AGENTS.md); (c) code is dead, unused, commented-out or debug-only; (d) a guard, else-branch or qualifier is redundant (`row()` already asserts; `public` in a struct). Every drop request names what to keep ('keeping the bf16 bit-exact round trip and partner-zero checks', 'keeping the kernel probes').

'please say so in the description' / 'narrow the docs' fires when a claim in the PR body, a Note, the README or a comment is wider than what the code does at this head, or is stale relative to it: T5 timed only on the HW join while docs say both; 'bare pointer is a compile error' true for V only; 'required CI builds AMX-off' while the workflow passes -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON; results from pre-merge commits; a section name that states the opposite of its assertion. He offers both repairs: change the code to match the docs, or narrow the docs.

'Nit:' / 'minor nit' / 'kinda pedantic' marks a point with no behaviour change that the author may decline: a name (section name, HW O vs Ra, descriptive param names), a key computed two ways, a duplicate test case, a redundant qualifier, constexpr placement, default-argument replication, order of two cheap checks. 14 comments carry the label.

'needs sign-off' / 'defer to <owner>' fires when a change touches a shared foundation outside the PR's subject and no test can catch a regression: a global `operator new[]` overload in a widely included header that arrived in a side commit rather than the owner's PR (ask the named maintainer for explicit sign-off); lock placement in the DMA layer (defer to the driver owner); a FUSE manifest extension (ask the stats owner). He names the person and does not block on his own authority.

'split them out' fires for changes that are not part of the PR's stated subject (AMX tile-number constants, a t_heap_v2 alignment check in a typed-tensors PR), for merge artifacts and for stray files; 'please squash' fires when the commit list carries rewrites of one item (20 commits, three rewording one Note).

Bot or agent findings are adjudicated by reachability first: trace the call graph; if the line cannot be reached with today's constants, models or callers, say so with the evidence, mark 'not a blocker', and open a STORY or follow-up; if reachable, fix it, add a regression test, and state why the fix is inert for current models; duplicate findings of a tracked bug are closed with the thread id.

'Design question' fires when a keying or granularity choice changes what a metric means in serving (per-forward class under continuous batching; rows keyed by attention index when thread mapping shifts): ask 'was this chosen on purpose?', give the concrete serving scenario where it misleads, offer two alternatives, and accept documentation of the narrower meaning as the fallback.

Tests follow three rules: extend the closest existing suite instead of adding a binary; a check that can silently skip on CI hosts (behind an `available()` early return) counts as no check and must move above the return or into an always-run suite; a test must observe the boundary where corruption would show (a fake that discards descriptors proves nothing about destinations).

Silent handling in production is rejected in favour of an assert or debug_exit: range guards that drop counts, early returns on bad input, unbounded spin loops, spin-waits that replace a tripwire; 'we can't meaningfully continue on with this right?' is the test.

Severity is stated explicitly in the comment: 'Not a stopper for this PR', 'Not blocking for this merge', 'No action needed, just inquiring', 'Fine as a first step', 'Coverage gap:', 'Confirmed real — fixed'. An approval can carry an open question (PR 4267 approved with the FUSE question; PR 4596 approved after the fixes).
register: Sentence shape: a declarative fact first, the consequence second introduced by 'So', the ask third ('Suggest dropping ...', 'Move it above the early return, or into t_llama_unit', 'please say so in the description'). Most inline comments are one to three sentences; long comments appear only for a bot refutation or a coverage gap.

Citation style: backticked identifiers plus a location in the same clause: '(line 197)', 'cmake-single-platform.yml:355', 'threading.hpp:741', commit SHAs (39a68994465f...), PR numbers (#4424, #4698), and repo policy by name ('AGENTS.md treats NaN as corruption', 'test policy'). Counts in the corpus: file:line in 16 comments, 'line N' in 14, SHAs in 10.

Asking: when the author's intent is unknown he asks rather than asserts: 'did you intend to leave this `return`?', 'was this intentional?', 'leaving enabled intentionally?', 'Was per-forward granularity chosen on purpose?', tag questions ending in 'right?'. 135 of 480 comments contain a question mark.

Mechanics: GitHub ```suggestion blocks (43 comments) for one-line edits to comment wording, typos, variable names and integer types; the suggestion is followed by one line of reason ('... right?', 'per line 1138 below').

Labels at the start of the comment: 'Nit:', 'Design question', 'Coverage gap:', 'minor nit', 'kinda pedantic', bold verdict leads in long comments ('**Not reachable as filed — but we're hardening the fragility it points at.**', '**Confirmed real — fixed.**').

Quantified claims: '20 commits, three of them rewording one Note', 'a 4096-token 36-layer prefill runs this ~4608 times', 'four near-verbatim copies', '48 allowlist violations (24 leaves x both scan modes)', '27 in your run ... 20 in your run'.

Options not orders: he gives two concrete repairs and lets the author choose ('Either time the SW poll too ..., or narrow the docs'; 'Move it above the early return, or into t_llama_unit'; 'keying by pool worker index ... Alternatively, record n_attn_workers per forward').

Transparent about AI drafting: 13 comments quote Claude, GPT or Codex verbatim ('I asked GPT to evaluate this... it agrees', 'Claude had this to say', 'Claude, Codex and my own analysis confirms'). From 2026-07 on his own comments take the same shape (bold verdict, bullets, file:line, no emoticons); the 2025-09 to 2026-06 comments are informal ('lol', ';p', 'drives me nuts'). The 4557 and 4596 comments match the later shape, consistent with agent-assisted drafting.

Tone: direct, no apology or praise padding (one 'I like the cleanup / refactor!' in 480); disagreement is stated plainly with evidence ('Cursorbot is wrong: ...', 'wrong... this populate method is used by the model code, here:') and softened only by the explicit severity label.
